title: Penn State announces captains for Week 3
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State's Week 3 captains have been announced.

Quarterback Rocco Becht, offensive lineman Anthony Donkoh and linebackers Kooper Ebel and Tony Rojas were named captains against Buffalo in the annual THON game.

Becht, Donkoh and Ebel have been staples of the captain list through two games while Rojas is making his debut wearing the "C."

The Nittany Lions host the Bulls at noon Saturday inside Beaver Stadium.

title: Penn State men’s soccer unable to outlast Michigan State in competitive matchup
author: Gavin Leonard | The Daily Collegian
description:
After a hard-fought back-and-forth battle, the Nittany Lions suffer their second loss in conference play of the season against the No.19 Michigan State Spartans.

After its loss to Washington on Sept. 11, Penn State looked to bounce back with a potential win versus a ranked opponent in its Big Ten opener.

While the blue and white proved that it could keep up with elite competition, Penn State’s inability to keep its foot on the gas for the entirety of the game became the downfall for coach Rob Dow’s squad.

To begin the match, both sides struggled to find their footing on the attacking end. Michigan State played a high line early, forcing the defenders to make quicker decisions, leading to dangerous passes.

Penn State played with both patience and pressure at different points during the opening minutes of the half, not allowing the Spartans to control the pace of play. Neither team had dominated possession at this point in the game, yet Michigan State had created a few more chances than the blue and white could.

Once both attacks settled in, opportunities started to develop. The Spartans began to control possession due to their ability to win back the ball even after losing it in the final third. When the Nittany Lions weathered the storm, the attack poured on.

The opening half did see a couple of near goals, including a cross sent in from the left followed by a misjudged header that grazed off the attacker's head. Nonetheless, Penn State went into halftime with momentum and tied up with a nationally ranked opponent.

“This team needs to learn how to win and convert in those moments, and take care of business,” coach Dow said. “We need to step up, make big plays.”

Coming out of the break, the blue and white carried the energy into the second half. The defense continued its persistence, winning the ball from pressuring on short goal kicks.

The defensive effort led to shot attempts on the other end, yet the attack could not finish. At one point, it seemed as if the Nittany Lions were due for a goal.

When Penn State continued to unsuccessfully convert chances, the Spartans would respond with counterattacks. However, the blue and white defense stood strong, putting an end to counters by blocking shot attempts and winning balls in the air.

A key moment during that stretch was a diving save from freshman goalkeeper Daniel Peluffo-Wiese.

With five minutes left, the defensive performance became obsolete, as Michigan State would score the game’s lone goal on a corner kick that landed back post. Penn State couldn't answer with a goal of their own, falling to 0-2 in Big Ten play.

“With 70 minutes left, we lost some gas,” coach Dow said. “It’s hard to swallow a loss like this, you know?”

title: A game to remember, Penn State men's soccer honors the late Mack Brady in a home match
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State returned to Jeffrey Field for its second conference competition under the lights on Friday night, taking on Michigan State for the team's annual Mack Brady Memorial match.

Michigan State entered the match ranked 19th in Division I and second in the Big Ten, giving the blue and white the opportunity to shine and show their potential against a strong opponent.

The Nittany Lions put up a strong fight, going back and forth with the Spartans until the end. Michigan State’s Oscar St. Huerta scored the game-winning goal and put the score at 1-0.

John William Mackenzie Brady was two weeks away from his ninth birthday before an unexpected blood infection led to his passing on New Year's Eve in 2012. A State College native, Mack loved soccer and had the dream of one day playing for Penn State as its goalkeeper.

"We had the family in the locker room before the game, understanding the legacy of Mack and the community of the club we play for, Celtic, and what our job is,” coach Rob Dow said. “To know we have a legacy, a community, and a state that’s behind us. So let’s go out there and be the best version of ourselves.”

After his tragic passing, Mack’s parents Elizabeth and Christian set up a memorial fund in his honor to benefit Penn State soccer and its goalkeeper program. The fund has been partnered with the team for over a decade to further the success of the program, and continue on Mack’s legacy.

The fund provides resources for the team to ensure players are getting the best experience and training they can at Penn State, and has contributed to the installation of the fields and facilities, while also providing goalkeepers with their clubs each year.

The stands were filled on Friday night as the blue and white kept the pressure on the Spartans, meeting them at every play they made. Penn State kept Michigan State off the board in the first half, with the defense standing tall, refusing to let the ball get past them.

At the half, the Brady family took the field to honor their son, remembering him as a loving individual who was passionate about friends, family, and his love of the game of soccer. Brady’s past soccer team, the Celtic Club, was also in attendance, doing a youth scrimmage before the start of the second half.

The Nittany Lions were relentless in the second half, ready to fight, seeing multiple corners and shot attempts by players such as Nehan Hassan and two tries from Arian St. Recinos, who was making his collegiate debut. A promising shot from junior forward Etienne Reck looked to be the first goal of the game as it was aimed towards the top of the net, but was saved by Michigan State goalkeeper Jake Grekowicz.

An incredible save by Nittany Lions’ netminder Daniel Pellufo-Wiese in the 79th minute kept the Spartans off the board. After this, it looked like the game was sure to end in a tie, as both teams continuously met each other's strength, speed and agility up and down the field.

With five minutes left on the board, St. Huerta scored the first, and only, goal of the game, putting the Spartans up by one and leaving little time for the blue and white to make a comeback.

“It’s so hard to swallow a loss like this, because they had three corners, we had seven, so we lose our mark, we don’t follow through,” Dow said. “This team needs to learn and convert in those moments and take care of business in critical times, especially with like five and change left in the game.”

Even with a loss, Friday night's matchup was about more than the game. The Nittany Lions' performance will be a good kickstarter for the team as they continue with conference play throughout the next seven games.

title: Penn State men's soccer drops game against Michigan State after late goal
author: Luci Palacios | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State returned to Jeffrey Field looking to put its loss behind them and get back on track in conference play. Starting with the Nittany Lions first home conference game, in an annual memorial for Mack Brady.

The blue and white entered Friday’s matchup against Michigan State at 2-3 following a 4-2 loss to the Washington Huskies, while the Spartans come in at 5-1-1 after shutting out Northwestern 2-0 this past Tuesday.

The Nittany Lions fall to Michigan State 1-0 at home in devastating fashion in the final minutes.

First half

The Nittany Lions came out attacking early, which rewarded them with their first corner of the game within two minutes. This led to their first shot by senior forward Amadou Kone, but it was off target.

It did not take long for the Spartans to respond, earning their first corner kick in the third minute of the game, along with their first shot taken by senior midfielder Miles Merritt, but that too was off target.

Penn State didn’t take its foot off the pedal and kept attacking, with Kone taking a shot in the bottom left of the net, but junior goalkeeper Jake Grekowicz made the save. Shortly after, Kone got another chance, but the defense blocked it early.

Michigan State gained control of the game and started to set up attacking opportunities through the midfield. They did make a breakthrough but were unable to get it in the box, resulting in a goal kick.

The game started to get physical in the 11th minute, with Kone committing the first foul and earning Charlie Norkett a free kick. Four minutes later, Norkett got fouled again outside the box by Vladislav Cherny, awarding another free kick.

The penalty kick was an try to set up a header on the right side of the box but was unsuccessful.

The aggressiveness continued with lots of slide tackles from the Penn State defense. Eventually, this resulted in the first yellow card of the game, given in the 18th minute to Grant McIntosh for unsportsmanlike conduct.

The Spartans maintained their presence in the Nittany Lion half for most of the first half, showing their determination to score.

But that was disrupted by freshman goalkeeper Daniel Peluffo-Wiese in the 26th minute with a crucial save and an otherwise dangerous collision with a Michigan State player. Both players were down for a while, but both were ok.

This physical matchup remained prevalent in the Penn State half, which resulted in another yellow card for unsporting behavior by the Nittany Lions in the 26th minute, this time given to Noah Förster. This penalty kick was taken just outside the box by Merritt, which skyrocketed over the net.

The Nittany Lions made their first breakthrough in a while in the 30th minute but couldn’t finish the play. The blue and white kept applying pressure, earning two corner kicks in a minute, but only one sniffed the goal.

Junior defender Arian Recinos created another opportunity up the left side of the field in the 36th minute with a cross in the box to junior Etienne Reck, who missed the header. The chances didn’t stop there, with Noah Andreas shooting a crossbar shot, and multiple coming shortly after, but still no goals.

After a fierce Nittany Lions’ attack, the Spartans fought back with their fourth shot of the game coming in the 43rd minute from Luke Spadafora that was off target.

As the half came to an end, the score was 0-0 with five shots from Penn State and four shots from Michigan State. This displayed how both teams fighting for that first goal.

Second half

Penn State came into this half with the same intensity as the first, with fans riled up with drums and encouraging shouts. It appeared to affect the Spartans as Merritt committed a foul on Nehan Hasan.

This does not disrupt the Nittany Lions offense as they continued to attack and create chances in the Michigan State half. Unfortunately, not able to capitalize on the opportunities but can stay in the Spartans' half.

Another goal-scoring chance presented itself for the blue and white as Hasan gets his head on the ball, but it is shot out-of-bounds.

The physicality continues from Penn State, as Recinos earned the third yellow card for the blue and white in the 57th minute for unsporting. Nine minutes later four fouls came from Penn State, one of which was another yellow card this time for Toby Grant in the 66th minute outside the box.

Penn State applied quick pressure as Reck heads the ball in the goal box in the 78th minute but is unsuccessful.

As the game came to an end, Michigan State earned a corner kick and capitalized on it in the 84th minute. A diving header by Oscar Huerta sealed it in the bottom left of the goal, making the score 1-0. Assists came from Merritt and Andrew Darakdijan, giving the Spartans the lead and the game. Huerta received a yellow card for unsporting behavior following the goal.

Penn State fell short 1-0 to Michigan State and dropped to 2-4 on the season and 0-2 in conference play. Michigan State improved to 6-1-1 overall and 2-0 in conference play.

Up next

Penn State travels to Bloomington, Indiana, to face the Hoosiers in conference play at 1 p.m.

title: Penn State women's volleyball earns 5th straight win, bests USF
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State earned its eighth win Friday night against USF, in a sweep. The Nittany Lions had momentum after coming off a 3-1 win against Villanova on Tuesday, where sophomore middle blocker Gabrielle Nichols led with 13 kills.

Penn State had a bit of an unsteady start after a reception error by Haley Burgdorf. The blue and white earned its first points after a Whitney Lauenstein kill to the back right to even out the momentum.

For the rest of the match, USF and Penn State traded single-digit leads. Nichols and Lauenstein put forth an effective front on the left side to force USF to call a timeout when the Nittany Lions earned their 11th point.

Nichols also paired well with Kennedy Martin on the right side, forcing USF to earn most of its points centrally. Finley Krystkowiak subbed in for Burgdorf and Penn State went on a three-point unanswered run, forcing USF to call another timeout.

USF kept attempting to crawl out of the small hole it dug itself in, but the Nittany Lion offense proved relentless and kept their lead to at least one until the conclusion of the set, where the blue and white won 25-18.

Nichols’ momentum carried onto the second set, giving the Nittany Lions their first three points off of two kills and a solo block.

USF went on a three-point run mid-set after a kill by junior Addy Brus and two service aces from middle blocker Amelia Wass de Czege. This spark was quickly counteracted after a kill by Martin, halting the lead from shifting in favor of the Bulls.

Following a kill by USF outside hitter Paula Tomasa and an attack error from Penn State’s Nichols, the Bulls were up by one. The remainder of the match saw a tight battle for the one-point upper hand.

“USF gave us some problems in serve receive,” coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley said.

Martin’s eighth kill of the match shifted the momentum back in the hands of the blue and white, while Lauenstein followed up with an ace of her own.

As the Nittany Lions earned their 18th point after a kill each from Martin and Ryla Jones, USF called a timeout, similar to the first set.

USF earned two more points before calling a second timeout, after a pair of kills from Alexis Stucky and Martin along with a service ace from Jones. Following the timeout, USF went on a four-point, unanswered run, and the Nittany Lions called for a timeout of their own.

“She feeds me really good balls,” Jones said. “She just instills a lot of confidence in me.”

USF earned the first point following the third timeout of the set, going up by one point. Nichols evened out the score with a kill and Lauenstein quickly followed with two of her own, for the Nittany Lions to take the lead at 24-22. Penn State took the second set after USF’s Emelyn Stettin committed a service error to award Penn State its 25th point.

USF got the first point of the third set after a Nittany Lion attack error. Two kills from Burgdorf and Lauenstein put the blue and white up by one point, but the score was quickly brought back to a tie following a Martin service error.

USF proceeded to go on a three-point run until Nichols put up two kills to even out the point difference. Penn State went on a three-point run of its own, forcing the Bulls to call a timeout. This didn’t halt Penn State’s energy, as they went on to put up two more points before a Finley service error.

Penn State remained in the lead until the 16th point of the set, when UCF’s Wass de Czege tied up the score following her service ace. Wass de Czege then committed a service error, keeping the score tied at 17-17.

The Bulls were able to earn their 18th point after Addy Brus’ kill to take the lead for the second time all match. The lead was short-lived, as Stettin committed a service error, and Krystkowiak then put up a kill to earn the blue and white their 19th point.

The rest of the set saw a competitive back-and-forth with the lead alternating between the Bulls and Nittany Lions.

“I thought Stucky did a good job of moving the ball around, and I thought both middles were involved, and Kennedy was finding ways to score,” Schumacher-Cawley said.

Martin put the blue and white within two points of a sweep win after her kill; however, a Burgdorf service error allowed the Bulls to take the offensive hand and tie up the score, leading to a Penn State timeout.

Following the timeout, Lauenstein put up a kill for the Nittany Lions 26th and match point. Despite the challenge, the original call stood and Penn State won the match in a sweep.

“It’s nice to win. It’s hard to win, and I’m just glad we found a way to finish that in three,” Schumacher-Cawley said.

Up Next

The Nittany Lions have a quick turnaround as they'll host Tennessee at noon on Saturday and at 2 p.m. on Sunday.

title: Penn State women's soccer keeps up offensive dominance in win versus Maryland
author: Zach Schroder | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State traveled to College Park to faceoff against the Maryland Terrapins for its third conference game of the season.

The Nittany Lions looked to keep an impressive streak alive; Maryland last beat Penn State in November 2004.

Ultimately, Penn State would defeat Maryland 2-0, staying dominant on the books.

1st Half

Senior forward Paige Kalal started the shots early, with a low-center placement at the 46-second mark of the match. The Paige’s were flipping as freshman midfielder Paige Pasinski had to back-to-back shots within 30 seconds around the four-minute mark; redshirt junior goalkeeper Faith Luckey saved one, while the other was blocked. Pasinski followed her oppressive attack with two more shots; Luckey saved both.

The Terraphins moved on offense quickly after, when sophomore forward McKinley Heaven nutmegged her defender and put a shot right below Penn State’s crossbar. Redshirt senior keeper Mackenzie Gress continued her amazing play this season with a jumping one-handed save to block Heaven’s goal attempt.

After an aggressive first 10 minutes from both sides, the game slowed a bit, with a couple of fouls and free kicks. After a throw-in by Maryland, the Nittany Lions took possession, and Kalal slammed a shot into the low-right side of the net to score the first goal of the game. Penn State led 1-0 at the 18-minute mark.

Both teams made their first substitutions in the 26th minute. There were six combined throw-ins in the six minutes after the subs came in, with both teams struggling to create anything meaningful. The cloud cover cleared in College Park while the heat and humanity clearly impacted the players.

Redshirt sophomore Jolie Farmer, a Penn State transfer, added some energy for the Terraphins off the bench. Maryland’s defense recovered from the early onslaught; it stonewalled any Nittany Lion offense in the latter part of the half. At the end of the half, the blue and white led in shots 7-2, with six of those being on goal.

2nd Half

Maryland’s offense looked more alive in the early minutes of the second half. On the other side of the pitch, the Nittany Lions had a free kick very close to the Terrapins' box that would lead to a corner, though Maryland staved them off.

The blue and white defenders played well against a couple of one-on-one and two-on-one breakaways. The Terrapins' intensity was clear compared to the first half. Senior forward and midfielder Lisa McIntyre had the first shot of the half for Maryland, but it soared far right of the net.

The Nittany Lions had a couple of wild shots in good scoring position, not being able to capitalize on their opportunities. Gress earned another save after a shot from junior defender and midfielder Ella Bulava.

Penn State returned that shot attempt with a couple of good passes. Like a good book, the Paige’s came alive again after Pasinski put one in the low-left corner; Kalal joined her with the assist. The blue and white led 2-0 in the 61st minute.

After a Nittany Lion goal kick, a challenge by head coach Erica Dambach gave them a penalty kick, but Aubrey Kulpa’s shot was saved by Luckey’s good read. Kulpa was then wrapped up by junior defender Dani Gichner, who was also responsible for the penalty earlier. Gichner received a yellow and was soon substituted for defender Sam Winer.

The Terrapins seemed to ramp up their aggression while down 2-0. Bulava drew another yellow quickly after the first. Senior defender Brooklyn Antonucci made a nice tackle, but took a little to get up, needing assistance from Gress, but she stayed in the match.

A Kulpa free kick soared into a nice header from redshirt sophomore defender Lilly Burger, but Luckey made a nice diving save in the middle of the posts. Maryland fought back after lots of time on their side of the pitch; Farmer’s pass to sophomore forward Abigail Stager missed wide left.

Farmer made her presence known again with a high center shot off an amazing ball from Drew Bernard; Gress with another save. Maryland head coach Michael Marchiano challenged, looking for a foul on Farmer, but the review found nothing.

The Nittany Lions staved off any Maryland offense to close the game.

Up next

The Nittany Lions will return to Happy Valley to face the Iowa Hawkeyes in the White Out at 7 pm on Jeffery Field.

title: Penn State Board of Trustees vote to sell Shenango, Wilkes-Barre campuses
author: Neel Ved | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Penn State Board of Trustees (BoT) voted in favor of selling the Penn State Shenango and Penn State Wilkes-Barre campuses on Friday. This comes a day after the Finance and Investment Committee approved the sale of the properties.

Trustees Cynthia Dunn, Russel Redding, and Carrie Rowe declined to vote on the sale of the campuses, while Robert Beard was not present for voting.

Penn State Shenango will be sold to JCL Development LLC for $1 million. The 13 acre property with 12 buildings will be used as a “hub for education, workforce training, economic development and cultural enrichment” according to a news release from Penn State.

The redevelopment aims to support reinvestment in the local community, including downtown Sharon, Pennsylvania.

“For the past 15 years, 'Team JCL' has worked to revive the spirit of our community, one project at a time,” JCL partners Jim Landino and Jen Krezeczowski said in the news release. “While the Penn State Shenango campus wasn't originally on our radar, we are excited to embrace this opportunity. We plan to bring new energy and innovative ideas to honor its rich history and continue our efforts to strengthen the Shenango Valley.”

Penn State Wilkes-Barre will be sold to HGC Development LLC, in partnership with Misericordia University, for $5.25 million. The property is 57 acres with 17 buildings.

HGC Development LLC is a subsidiary of Huntsville Golf Club and plans to turn the property into a multi-use site. This is slated to include an educational hub along with an event and conference venue.

"We see this as an opportunity to preserve something important to Northeastern Pennsylvania and maintain the current nature of the property," Angelo Terrana, an attorney representing HGC Development LLC, said in the news release. "It offers new opportunities for an exciting future."

Both campuses will remain open until the end of the spring 2027 semester, after which Shenango and Wilkes-Barre, along with five other Commonwealth Campuses, will close.

Penn State Shenango currently has 300 students enrolled, while Penn State Wilkes-Barre has 350.

In their news release, Penn State said “Neither transaction changes Penn State’s previously announced commitments to students, faculty and staff.”

title: Court documents reveal new details about alleged drug-ring; pledges required to pass 'steady hand test'
author: Grace Levy | News Editor
description:
Newly released court documents revealed details about how Delta Upsilon pledges allegedly helped package and distribute cocaine in Penn State's alleged cocaine trafficking ring.

The pledges were recruited by Thomas M. Robinson, one of the ring’s alleged leaders, during the spring and fall 2024 semesters. At this time, Robinson held various leadership roles at Delta Upsilon, including new member educator and president of academics.

Pledge involvement

According to testimony in the grand jury presentment, Robinson had “senior status” in the fraternity, giving him greater influence over pledges. Pledges testified that he was “calling the shots,” and working with the pledgemasters rather than acting as a mediator like the new member educator role intended.

Pledge Daniel Price testified to being recruited by Robinson to deliver cocaine to the Alpha Gamma Rho fraternity during the spring 2024 semester. Price allegedly delivered cocaine 10 times for Robinson. Afterwards, Price was asked to recruit another pledge, Kyle Ridpath, to work with Robinson.

Price and Ridpath were both charged with misdemeanors on Aug. 17 in connection to the case.

Price and Ridpath then joined Robinson in his room in the fraternity house where Robinson instructed them to purchase items intended for preparing and packaging cocaine.

After purchasing the items, Price and Ridpath returned to the house where Robinson showed a “semi solid brick” of what appeared to be cocaine. Robinson then demonstrated breaking the cocaine and cutting it with creatine. Price and Ridpath then measured the cocaine mix into half-gram bags, as instructed by Robinson.

Price estimated that they prepared between 200 to 300 half-gram bags of cocaine, according to the presentment.

Detective Donald Paul testified that Ridpath’s statements to police mirrored Price’s.

“He (Ridpath) eventually learned that Adderall, cocaine and marijuana were present at the DU house and anyone who lived there or spent time there was aware of the drugs,” the presentment read.

In spring 2025, Price learned of additional Delta Upsilon pledges who similarly assisted Robinson in preparing and distributing cocaine. Those pledges were Seth Beardsley, Charlie Weisman and Luke Lengel. Beardsley and Weisman have been charged with misdemeanors in connection to the case, while Lengel has not.

Weisman testified in the presentment that while pledging Delta Upsilon during the fall 2024 semester, Robinson contacted him and asked him to recruit two other pledges who were “trustworthy.”

Weisman recruited Beardsley and an unnamed pledge. Robinson allegedly instructed them to hold out their hands, and if they were steady enough, they would assist Robinson with an undisclosed task. Weisman and Beardsley passed the “steady hand test,” while the other pledge did not. Another pledge, Lengel, was then recruited to assist.

The three pledges were then allegedly instructed to print and sign copies of a non-disclosure form, which Robinson then tore up and threw away, according to the presentment.

Beardsley, Weisman and Lengel then allegedly assisted Robinson in preparing cocaine in Delta Upsilon’s boiler room, testifying that they packaged between 100 to 200 half-gram bags. This preparation occurred again on two other occasions.

Another unnamed pledge testified that he delivered cocaine outside of the fraternity on three separate occasions for Robinson.

Knowledge among Delta Upsilon brothers

Price testified that Delta Upsilon brother Ryan Matson and three unnamed pledge masters came in and out of Robinson’s room while the packaging occurred and “no one seemed surprised."

Matson testified during the preliminary hearing of Robinson’s father, Paul Robinson, on Sept. 3. Matson has not been charged in connection to the case.

Matson also testified in the grand jury presentment.

“Everyone in the fraternity knew Robinson supplied Adderall, marijuana and cocaine if anyone wanted to purchase it,” Matson was reported saying in the presentment.

Matson testified that he assisted Robinson in preparing cocaine for distribution and that Robinson brought up the idea of having pledges prepare the cocaine. He said that he and other Delta Upsilon brothers helped deliver and sell cocaine inside and outside the fraternity.

He also shared that people in the fraternity had told Robinson they were worried his operation was getting too big and was exposing himself and others to being arrested. Robinson allegedly ignored this and expanded his customer base to non-fraternity members.

Various brothers and pledges testified to the expectation that to “stay with the fraternity, they stay loyal to the fraternity.”

This includes the “unspoken rule” that no one talks about what goes on at the fraternity and no one reports what happens to law enforcement or PSU regardless of the situation.

They testified that this mentality existed for the dealing and usage of drugs at Delta Upsilon, which was not disclosed to anyone outside the fraternity, especially law enforcement or PSU administration.

Delta Upsilon brothers also testified in the presentment that the day after Robinson’s arrest, the incoming and outgoing Delta Upsilon presidents held a meeting for fraternity members. At the meeting, they shared Robinson's arrest and that anyone involved with Robinson “should get a lawyer and not talk to police.” They also instructed fraternity members to share with them if contacted by law enforcement.

Other fraternities mentioned

Two additional fraternities were mentioned in the documents: Phi Kappa Tau and Alpha Gamma Rho. Prior to this, three current fraternities — Delta Upsilon, Sigma Chi, Acacia — and one former fraternity — Sigma Alpha Mu — were mentioned.

Robinson testified to the grand jury that as he began dealing drugs at Delta Upsilon, an unnamed friend and member of Phi Kappa Tau shared information about where to get better marijuana at a cheaper price.

The friend shared details of a Native American reservation in Salamanca, New York, and accompanied Robinson to the reservation in spring 2023. There, Robinson purchased marijauna for himself, as well as to sell to others. He testified in the presentment that he could make a profit of between $1,500 and $1,800 per pound.

Robinson’s friend later introduced him to the app “Telegram” where he could get marijuana shipped from California directly to the fraternity house. With this, they avoided the risks associated with transporting the marijuna to Penn State themselves.

During one trip to New York, Robinson told his friend that someone selling cocaine was turning the business over to him and asked him to be his partner. The friend declined and said “he was in way over his head,” according to the presentment.

Robinson shared with the friend that he sold to members of other fraternities. Later in the presentment, Delta Upsilon pledge Price testified that Robinson directed him to deliver cocaine to an unnamed friend at the Alpha Gamma Rho fraternity, receiving $40.

Both Phi Kappa Tau and Alpha Gamma Rho are members of the Penn State Interfraternity Council, meaning they are recognized by Penn State and are affiliated with the university.

Alpha Gamma Rho was previously placed on organizational suspension from Jan. 2024 to Aug. 2024 for hosting an unauthorized event. They have not been suspended since.

title: Penn State field hockey earns 2 US camp invitations
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
Two Penn Staters are going camping with the national team.

Aby Deverka and Olivia Marthins were invited to participate in the U.S. junior national team camp, USA Field Hockey announced Thursday.

It’s familiar territory for Deverka, a Houston, Texas, native, who participated in the U21 camp last season before ultimately earning a place on the junior national team. The junior goalkeeper has started every game for the Nittany Lions since the start of her sophomore season.

Marthins, a second-year midfielder/forward, appeared in all 17 games for the blue and white last season and has appeared in all six so far this year. The Haddonfield, New Jersey, native scored two goals in 2026, including one against then-No. 5 Virginia.

The camp will take place from Dec. 11 to Dec. 13 at Davidson College, and the team roster will be announced shortly after.

title: Meet Jaxon Eichelberger, the ‘Kickoff Kid’ for Penn State’s Week 3 game against Buffalo
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Jaxon Eichelberger was only 19 months old when he was diagnosed with High-Risk B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) in March 2020. Now he’s eight years old, over four years in remission and will serve as the Kickoff Kid on Saturday as Penn State takes on Buffalo at Beaver Stadium in the THON game.

As the Kickoff Kid, Eichelberger will get to run on the field and retrieve the kicker’s tee in front of over 100,000 fans. During halftime, Four Diamonds families walk on the field with signs saying “Go State Beat Cancer” in support of raising funds and awareness to combat pediatric cancer.

“We are beyond excited, and especially with it being the THON game that he gets to be the Kickoff Kid,” Kayla Eichelberger, Jaxon’s mother, told The Daily Collegian. “We've gone the last three years to the THON football game, and it is just so fun. Being able to run out and get that experience is going to be next level for him.”

Eichelberger’s diagnosis was aligned with the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, adding an additional layer of difficulty to his treatment process. Kayla was 36 weeks pregnant with his younger sister, Rylie, who was born that April.

He experienced cold-like symptoms and was on antibiotics, but his condition wasn’t getting any better. After a blood test, Kayla received a phone call of his diagnosis from her son’s pediatrician, and he was immediately admitted to Penn State Health Hershey Medical Center. The family stayed there for 10 days.

One of the chemotherapy medications that he was taking early on caused his voice to become raspy, and there were concerns of vocal cord paralysis, causing Eichelberger to miss the first month of treatment.

Eichelberger was readmitted to the hospital after four days at home, diagnosed with bacterial meningitis, and he was inpatient for an additional two weeks. It was during that time Rylie was born.

After 28 days of initial treatment, Eichelberger entered remission. He started his frontline and maintenance treatments, being readmitted to the hospital a number of times for fevers and infections before “ringing the bell” on Aug. 5, 2022. In July, he’ll officially be considered cured.

Looking back, Kayla said the most powerful thing about her son was his positive outlook.

“I always go back to a quote, kids are so resilient,” Kayla said. “Towards the end of his treatment in April 2022, he had been inpatient for about three weeks with another infection. When we were leaving, I said, ‘Buddy, I'm so sorry, we've been stuck in the hospital for three weeks.’ He said, ‘Don't worry, Mom, we're going home now.’”

Four Diamonds first brought up THON in 2021, during Eichelberger’s maintenance treatment. Kayla and her husband, Shane, knew about THON from a young age, as they participated in “Mini THONs” in high school, but they didn’t know the intricacies of being involved.

The Eichelberger family was paired with Phi Gamma Nu and attended their first THON at the Bryce Jordan Center in 2023.

Kayla said that her son was so young during his treatment that he doesn’t remember too much of it, something she feels fortunate for. Today, he’s as energetic and outgoing as ever, has a lot of friends and plays travel soccer.

“Jaxon is very spunky,” Kayla said. “He definitely has a lot of personality. He likes to be a goofball, hanging out with his friends, being outside, going fishing, riding his bike, but his favorite thing right now is he's on the travel soccer team, so he's excited to play.”

However, she wants her son to learn lessons from the experiences he gained and the people he met during his treatment, including the members of Phi Gamma Nu.

“I hope that he knows about all of the good that people put into him, and then turns around and puts it back into the world,” Kayla said.

The Eichelberger family hasn’t just attended the THON themed football games, though. On Sept. 4, they watched the men’s soccer THON game against Yale at Jeffrey Field with a group of 20 Phi Gamma Nu fraternity brothers.

Kayla said the most important part of having THON-themed games is reminding people that there are bigger things than sports, and putting that into perspective makes a substantial difference.

“Having that reminder for people, I think is really cool,” Kayla said. “This is something the students at Penn State are doing that's bigger than them, bigger than football.”

title: Community Ofrenda welcomed everyone in celebration of Hispanic Heritage Month
author: Sarah Price | The Daily Collegian
description:
On Thursday, Sept. 17, The Paul Robeson Cultural Center (PRCC), located in the HUB-Robeson Center, hosted a Community Ofrenda, where people came together to celebrate their loved ones who passed away in honor and remembrance. An ofrenda is a temporary altar built to welcome the deceased, and the word translates from Spanish into “offering.”

For the opening of the Community Ofrenda, there was a DJ who played Hispanic-inspired music, as well as complementary Venezuelan food from Juana’s Venezuelan Cuisine. This included traditional food items such as chicken and beef empanadas and tequeños.

“I feel like there’s not really too much Latino representation, and so I thought seeing [the ofrenda], was like, ‘Oh my god, what’s going on,’” Emeli Jarama-Morocho, a third-year studying pre-med, said.

Some students who came to the PRCC were drawn in by the music, as they could hear it from afar. Others were attracted by the energy the event brought.

“Everybody seems happy, and I’m friends with some of the people here, so it’s a wonderful celebration that brings people together,” Suri Phung, a PRCC liaison on the justice and equity board, said.

When people saw the ofrenda on display, as Shanna Lennox, a third-year studying chemistry, said, they stayed for the vibes and the food.

“The food was good, it definitely brought me back to home a little bit,” Christina Martinez, a student of Hispanic heritage, said.

On the altar, there was a gratitude and remembrance jar for attendees to participate in the tradition of the ofrenda. From the afterlife, the spirits of the loved ones visit the ofrenda to enjoy some of the things they loved while on Earth, according to the tradition. Some attendees were able to write a note to someone in their life who passed on and place it in the jar.

“I chose to write about my grandma, and I kind of shared about what’s happening with my life and why I’m here, and why I’m hiding,” Phung, a second-year studying political science, said.

The ofrenda was festively decorated with red, orange and yellow flowers, as well as a few small decorations like candles and calaveras throughout. These ornaments complimented the numerous framed photos of loved ones on the altar. Some loved ones were honored with food items near their photo such as honey, mango and tajin.

Martinez, a third-year studying human development and family studies, said she typically sits outside the PRCC in between classes but decided to come in when she realized there was a celebration happening.

“It was really cool to be able to see my heritage celebrated,” Martinez said. “And just see the recognition of the things that are very important this month.”

The ofrenda will be on display in the PRCC until Oct. 9.

title: Penn State vs. Buffalo preview | How to watch, betting odds and more
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State will welcome Buffalo to Beaver Stadium for the fourth time in program history and the first since 2019 at noon on Saturday.

It’ll be the fourth ever meeting between the Nittany Lions and Bulls, dating back to a 1900 meeting in Buffalo in which the Bulls won 10-0.

Penn State holds a 3-1 lead in the series and is currently on a three-game winning streak.

Here’s more information on the weather, betting odds and a look at both teams ahead of the Week 3 matchup.

Forecast

With the noon kickoff, the sun will be out in full force leading up to and into the start of the game, according to AccuWeather.

The temperature will be a high of 71 degrees, with a real feel high of 74 before clouds start to form as the afternoon goes on.

There's a chance of a late-afternoon or early evening shower that shouldn’t affect the game, but could impact travelers or postgame tailgaters.

Betting, how to watch

The sportsbooks are anticipating a blowout in favor of Penn State, the largest of the season by a significant margin.

The Nittany Lions will enter as a 40.5 point favorite over the Bulls, according to FanDuel. The over-under is set at 49.5 points.

The game will air on Big Ten Network, with tickets available for the game as low as $15 on Ticketmaster.

About Buffalo

Buffalo is coming off a 33-20 loss to FIU in Week 2, moving to 1-1 on the season following a 21-17 win over Albany in the opening week.

The Bulls haven’t found a full answer at quarterback yet, and with an injury to initial starter Elijah Holmes that’s gone into the week of practice, it’s likely that Jason Wright will get the starting nod for his team’s toughest game of the season.

When Wright entered in Week 2, Buffalo was already trailing big, but his efforts made it closer than how the game was trending prior to the half. Wright continued to find the Bulls’ top target, Chase Morrow, who accounts for 34% of their entire offensive production.

Morrow has 218 receiving yards this year, nearly 200 more than the next highest. He’s also the only offensive player to have a touchdown to his name, finding the end zone five times through two weeks.

On the defensive side, it’s a story of lack of production for Buffalo. As a whole, it totaled just three sacks and two turnovers through two weeks against two teams that are closer to its competition.

Against a team like Penn State, it’ll have to come up with bigger plays that it’s yet to do with consistency, with linebacker Stevie Bracey and cornerback SaVeon Brown as the likely candidates to make those plays. The duo are tied for second with tackles on the team, with Bracey forcing a fumble against FIU.

About Penn State

The Nittany Lions close out their nonconference schedule against statistically the worst team of the three they’ve faced, with Buffalo ranked right below Marshall on ESPN’s FPI.

Penn State’s pass game has performed at a high level through two games, led by quarterback Rocco Becht, who has 539 passing yards on a 75.6% completion percentage without turning over the ball.

Becht’s top target, Koby Howard, has 229 yards receiving and has proven to be a deep threat target. He’s joined by the top touchdown target, tight end Benjamin Brahmer, who’s accumulated three touchdowns in two games.

The passing game has covered up some of the struggles in the run game for Penn State, as the rushers have combined for 3.9 yards per carry. Running back Carson Hansen has 132 rushing yards with 4.4 yards per carry and has yet to break off a big run.

On defense, Tony Rojas has led the way following his return from a long-term injury suffered last year. Rojas has stuffed the stat sheet with 14 total tackles, a sack and an interception.

The defensive backs have limited opposing offenses to 105 yards per game in the air, which ranks fourth in the country. The plethora of defensive backs the Nittany Lions can put out together likely means high opportunities to prevent the Buffalo passing game from getting any momentum going.

Injury updates

Penn State continues to get healthier as Matt Campbell has provided updates to previously injured players.

Defensive tackles Alijah Carnell and Armstrong Nnodim will be back and make their Penn State debuts against Buffalo on Saturday.

Linebacker Cam Smith is currently a “question mark,” according to Campbell, but he practiced Tuesday. Smith was the fourth linebacker in the opener and didn’t play in the win over Temple.

Penn State will be without defensive end Max Granville for the rest of the season after Campbell confirmed last Saturday that Granville suffered a season-ending injury during practice leading up to the Nittany Lions’ game against Temple.

title: Players to watch | WR Chance Morrow, young QB among Buffalo’s Week 3 notable
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State hosts Buffalo in its final nonconference game of the 2026 season, marking the last chance for the Nittany Lions to tune up for the Big Ten slate.

The Bulls’ offensive system is dominated by a star wide receiver who’s now being fed passes by the team’s young backup quarterback in the wake of Elijah Holmes’ knee injury.

While the odds are overwhelmingly in Penn State’s favor, here are some names to know on the Buffalo side going into Week 3.

Chance Morrow, wide receiver

Chance Morrow waited four years for his opportunity to be a go-to receiver. After redshirting in his true freshman season at Louisville, he transferred to Buffalo and primarily held a depth role, tallying 16 receptions in three years.

But now, Morrow makes up the bulk of the Bulls’ firepower, contributing 34% of the Bulls’ offensive yards so far. He’s gotten off to a hot start, accumulating 218 receiving yards and all five of Buffalo’s touchdowns this season.

Despite losing to FIU last week, Morrow had 170 yards on 11 catches with a pair of touchdowns.

Morrow is difficult to guard one-on-one, as he uses his 6-foot-4 frame and long arms to haul in lob passes even when he’s under heavy coverage.

The Bulls may look to pass even more now that starting running back Terrance Shelton Jr. is out with an arm injury for four to six weeks, per Marquel Slaughter of The Buffalo News.

Penn State’s defensive secondary limited Temple to 107 passing yards on 13 receptions in Week 2, not allowing a single catch over 15 yards. With Morrow’s strength bringing in the deep ball, the backfield will get a different look than in previous matchups.

Jason Wright, quarterback

Holmes has dealt with knee problems that flared up in the game against FIU, and he didn’t practice on Tuesday, per Jonah Bronstein of the Associated Press. That means redshirt freshman Jason Wright may make his first collegiate start at Beaver Stadium.

Wright relieved Holmes in the second quarter and drew a lot of attention, including from Matt Campbell on Wednesday. Campbell said the Bulls “found themselves a great quarterback in the second half.”

Wright’s connection with Morrow was key to Buffalo’s attempted comeback, connecting on a pair of touchdowns.

However, his season debut was inconsistent, as he went 13-for-27 for 185 yards with an interception and fumble.

There was a glimpse at Wright’s dual-threat capabilities, as he ran into the end zone through contact for a gritty 2-point conversion.

Penn State struggled to contain Jaxon Smolik in the run game last week, so Wright may give the Nittany Lions another chance to lock down a mobile quarterback.

Stevie Bracey, linebacker

Buffalo’s top linebacker, Stevie Bracey, transferred from Virginia, where he’d spent the last four seasons. Bracey missed 2024 with a torn meniscus suffered in fall camp before appearing in two games the following year.

In 2023, Bracey played in 11 games and made one start, leading the Cavaliers with 10 tackles against a ranked Tennessee team in the season opener. He finished with 26 tackles and a tackle for loss in 20 games at Virginia.

Bracey is now fully healthy, and he hasn’t looked back. He has 16 tackles with two tackles for loss and a sack.

With the Nittany Lions’ run game being an area of concern, look out for Bracey as he attempts to thwart Penn State’s running backs.

SaVeon Brown, cornerback

SaVeon Brown operates at the nickel spot and has seen some success shutting down the middle of the field. He has started his redshirt senior campaign on the right foot with 16 tackles on the season, including a 10-tackle performance against FIU.

Brown also had a solid showing against UAlbany with six tackles. However, his biggest play of the game was a diving interception in the third quarter, the Bulls’ first and only pick so far this season.

He also serves as one of Buffalo’s kick returners, with his lone attempt coming midway through the first quarter against FIU, which he returned for a team-high 20 yards.

Brown’s athleticism may be one of Rocco Becht’s biggest obstacles Saturday if he’s looking to find wide receiver Koby Howard in the slot.

title: Penn State women's basketball releases Big Ten schedule
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Penn State Lady Lions women's basketball team has announced their 2026-27 Big Ten schedule.

The Lady Lions will start conference play Dec. 6 in East Lansing, Michigan, against Michigan State. Penn State will then have a 23-day break from conference play until the squad plays Purdue Dec. 29 in State College.

Two days later, to start the new calendar year, the team will take on Oregon on New Year's Day.

Tanisha Wright's squad will then travel to Minnesota to play the Golden Gophers Jan. 5, where Penn State will face former Lady Lion Gracie Merkle, who was the blue and white’s second leading scorer a season ago.

Four days later, the Lady Lions will start their two-game home-and-away series against Rutgers in State College and then end the week playing Indiana on Jan. 12.

The team will then head out west to play defending national champion UCLA on Jan. 15 and USC on the 18th.

On Jan. 24, the blue and white play Michigan, a team that reached the Elite Eight a season ago, in Ann Arbor before heading back to State College to close out the month of January against Ohio State.

To start the month of February, the team plays at Northwestern on the 4th and then plays Maryland on the 7th at home. The Lady Lions will then head to New Brunswick to finish the season series against Rutgers on Feb. 10.

Three days later, the Washington Huskies will pay a visit, followed by Iowa on Feb. 18. The following week, the Lady Lions will finish conference play against Nebraska on the 21st, Illinois on the road on the 25th and will close out their regular season against Wisconsin at home on the 28th.

title: Penn State field hockey drops second straight game, falls to No. 5 Maryland in Big Ten opener
author: Owen Lomotan I The Daily Collegian
description:
Following a narrow 2-1 loss to the Princeton Tigers on Sept. 13, Penn State looked to bounce back in its first conference game of the season against the No.5 Maryland Terrapins on Thursday at home for the annual THON game.

The Nittany Lions couldn’t overcome the Terrapins offensive dominance, as they fell to the Terrapins 4-1 in regulation.

The opening moments of the game were back-and-forth between both sides.

With 13:43 to go in the first, Maryland earned its first penalty corner.

Junior goalkeeper Aby Deverka and the Nittany Lion defense were able to stop Maryland right at the net, keeping the score even at nothing apiece.

Both Maryland and the Nittany Lions played into each other’s hands until the Terrapins struck first with 9:32 remaining in the first quarter from a shot by sophomore Midfielder Brinkley Eyre.

Maryland’s next shot attempt came with just over six minutes left in the frame, but was no good, leaving the score 1-0.

The Terrapins kept up the pressure, keeping Penn State on its heels as the first quarter winded down.

Junior forward Ella Gaitan was given a green card with 1:40 remaining, presenting an opportunity for Maryland to put on some pressure as the opening frame was almost at its close.

With 1:07 remaining, Maryland was given its second penalty corner. Deverka came up with a big save to keep the blue and white’s deficit at one score.

The second quarter for Penn State began with a shot by freshman forward Chloe D’Hage with 10:35 remaining, but that attempt was unsuccessful.

Gaitan’s shot with just under nine minutes remaining went wide over the target, keeping Penn State down a goal.

The Terrapins were given a third penalty corner with 7:26 remaining in the first half. The Nittany Lion defense stood firm, keeping Maryland from extending its lead.

A green card was given to Maryland sophomore midfielder Maia Adamson with 39 seconds remaining in the second quarter.

The first half came to a close after physical back-and-forth play from both sides, and the deficit remained one goal for the Nittany Lions.

The opening minutes of the second half were tight and physical between the two sides.

The Nittany Lions were given their first penalty corner of the game with 9:19 remaining in the third quarter. The blue and white capitalized on this opportunity as a goal from Gaitan, a Maryland transfer, tied up the score at one goal apiece.

With 13:40 remaining in the fourth quarter, junior forward Babs van Hest broke the tie for Maryland as the Terrapins took a 2-1 lead in the early portions of the final frame.

It didn’t take too long for Maryland to find a net again as the Terrapins continued their offensive dominance with their third goal of the game coming from freshman midfielder Ella Beach. This extended the Terrapins lead to 3-1 over the Nittany Lions with just under nine minutes remaining.

As the rain began to fall, Maryland scored once again, extending its goal count to four, after senior forward Maci Bradford found the back of the net with just under five minutes remaining.

Bradford’s goal was the final of the Terrapins scoring train as the fifth-ranked team in the country was ultimately too big of a match for Penn State.

“At halftime, we really focused on making some tactical changes that were necessary and just getting them to lock in,” coach Hannah Prince said. “It was obviously a close game, we were disappointed with some of the decision making in the first half but they made those adjustments in the third quarter so can’t blame them for that.”

Up Next

The Nittany Lions will travel to face No. 19 Monmouth on Sunday for the start of their first away-game stretch of the season.

title: Penn State trustees to approve sale of Penn State Shenango, Wilkes-Barre
author: Grace Levy | News Editor
description:
A Penn State Board of Trustees committee advanced plans to sell Penn State Shenango and Wilkes-Barre on Thursday. The full Board of Trustees (BoT) will vote on the sale on Sept. 18.

The Finance and Investment Committee voted to sell the Shenango property to JCL Development LLC for $1 million and Wilkes-Barre property to HGC Development LLC for $5.25 million.

The plans are the first proposed sales since the BoT announced the closure of seven Commonwealth Campuses in May 2025. The campuses are set to close at the end of the spring 2027 semester.

"Penn State has worked, throughout this process, to strike a responsible balance between stewarding the University's resources and honoring our commitment to each campus community, including Shenango and Wilkes-Barre," Renata Engel, vice president for Commonwealth Campuses and executive chancellor, said in a press release. "Both proposals outline a vision for preserving the community-facing qualities of these properties while building on the educational impact the campuses have had for decades, and that's an outcome we're pleased to see reflected in each plan."

title: Penn State wrestling earns 4 top-ranked wrestlers in preseason InterMat rankings
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
The wrestling season is almost here.

InterMat unveiled its preseason weight-class rankings for the upcoming 2026-27 season. The rankings featured four No. 1 Penn Staters and multiple projected weight-class changes.

Reigning 125-pound champion Luke Lilledahl will begin his season as the top-ranked wrestler. Lilledahl went undefeated in his sophomore season.

At 133 pounds, Marcus Blaze will begin his sophomore campaign as the No. 4-ranked wrestler. Blaze finished 4th at the NCAA Championships and will begin ranked behind the other three of the freshman standouts at the weight class from a year ago.

Braeden Davis represents Penn State at 141 pounds. Davis ranks at No. 9 in the preseason rankings, but there are expectations that Masanosuke Ono could fill the spot for his lone year of eligibility.

At 149 pounds, Shayne Van Ness will begin as the No. 4 wrestler in the weight class. Van Ness is behind Stanford's Aden Valencia, who defeated the Nittany Lion in the title match, and two returners who weren't in the weight class a year ago — Virginia Tech's Caleb Henson and Oklahoma State's Sergio Vega.

Tyler Kasak makes his return to the rankings after redshirting a season ago. Kasak ranks No. 2 behind reigning champion Landon Robideau of Oklahoma State.

At 165 pounds, PJ Duke is the top-ranked wrestler at a new weight class. It's not fully confirmed yet whether Duke is making the jump to 165 pounds, but no matter where he slots in, he's expected to be a favorite to stand atop the podium in March.

Also making a jump in weight class in the InterMat rankings, Mitchell Mesenbrink slots in at No. 1 at 174 pounds. Mesenbrink has wrestled at 165 pounds in the past three years, losing only once in his three-year career at Penn State.

At 184 pounds, Rocco Welsh will begin his redshirt junior season at No. 2, only behind Minnesota's Max McEnelly, who won the NCAA title over Welsh.

Josh Barr will attempt to defend his 2025 title at 197 pounds. He begins the 2025-26 season as the top-ranked wrestler at his weight. Rounding out the weight classes, heavyweight Cole Mirasola begins at No. 6 to start his sophomore campaign.

title: Penn State's veteran LBs thriving with communication, playmaking through 2 weeks
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
When Cael Brezina was a true freshman at Iowa State, he took the field at MIKE linebacker wearing the green dot.

That responsibility is often reserved for a veteran player on the field. However, the young linebacker earned that role numerous times during his two years at Iowa State, as well as against Temple last weekend. His “voice that projects” has helped get the team on the same page before every snap.

“I’m pretty comfortable with (the green dot),” Brezina said Wednesday. “I think a lot of the time, you know you’re using it to get the call, but a lot of the time you’re signaling anyway.”

While Brezina isn’t one of Penn State’s starting two linebackers, he’s embraced the opportunity to lead the defense. He’s been a dominant threat against opposing offenses, recording the second-most tackles on the team through two games.

“I’m just able to process and react really fast,” Brezina said. “That’s been a cool thing that I’ve noticed, whether it’s the defense or just having more experience as a football player.”

Outside of Brezina, Tony Rojas and Kooper Ebel have led the way in the linebacker room, starting the first two weeks of the season.

Ebel came to Happy Valley from Iowa State, where he was one of Matt Campbell’s go-to defenders. Although he hasn't filled the stat sheet like Rojas and Brezina, he's served as the defense’s primary communicator — a duty he had with the Cyclones.

However, his leadership has gone beyond his on-field communication, as he’s been a role model for the younger linebackers.

“I’ve played with Kooper for a long time,” Brezina said. “One thing that has always stood out about him is just consistency. It’s why you see him as a captain on Saturdays.”

Ebel’s work ethic has earned him a starting role in Campbell’s defense in every game since his sophomore year, amassing 28 starts so far. He’s had a slower start to the 2026 season as compared to others, but has been aided by Rojas.

After tearing his ACL last October, Rojas’ recovery lasted well into the spring months, keeping him off the field as other players learned new defensive coordinator D’Anton Lynn’s schemes and playcalling.

Despite his delay in taking the field, Rojas has been arguably the best defender for Penn State through two games.

“He’s very motivated,” cornerback Daryus Dixson said. “He’s trying to stop whoever is coming at us.”

Rojas leads the team with 14 tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and an interception. Against Temple, he showcased his multiplicity on the field, rushing the passer, dropping back into coverage and stopping the run.

“He’s talented in all aspects of the game,” Brezina said. “He’s able to do a lot of different things, super athletic.”

While Penn State’s offense is centered around the tight ends, the veteran linebackers have played a critical role in the defense, which is currently ranked No. 15 nationally.

title: Penn State men’s basketball drops 2026-27 season schedule
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
With fall just around the corner, it’s only a matter of time before the winter is here, and basketball is back. Penn State men's basketball officially has this season's slate set in stone.

As part of a conference-wide special on the Big Ten Network revealing the whole slate, Penn State fans now have a glimpse at the completed 2026-27 Big Ten schedule.

Penn State opens the Big Ten slate in Happy Valley on Dec. 8 with Nebraska heading to town, as only four days later the blue and white begin road conference play in Illinois.

The Nittany Lions then embark on a three-game nonconference stretch before facing Oregon, Minnesota, Northwestern and Wisconsin in an alternating stretch of home and away games. After that the blue and white face a gauntlet with consecutive games against Ohio State, Purdue, Iowa, Michigan State, Maryland and Indiana before again facing the Buckeyes.

Mike Rhoades’ squad then heads to Cornhuskers’ territory to complete the home-and-away series, which joins the scarlet and gray and Rutgers as the two-play opponents for Penn State this season.

To wind down the regular season, the blue and white host Washington and Michigan before road tests against UCLA and USC.

The Nittany Lions went 12-20 last season and 3-17 in the Big Ten under head coach Mike Rhoades and will have a major opportunity to re-establish themselves in the conference.

The team will play a total of 32 regular-season games before fighting for a spot in the NCAA tournament, after finishing in the second round during their last run in 2023.

title: Penn State men's soccer notebook | Rob Dow talks Mack Brady Match, Michigan State
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State kicked off its Big Ten slate on the West Coast last week, which left the blue and white with a losing record in its early season.

With a return to Happy Valley for the conference opener looming, first-year coach Rob Dow met with the media post-practice on Wednesday to discuss the dire stretch for his Nittany Lions.

Here is what was discussed.

Mack Brady match

Coming off a loss against Wisconsin in their first conference match, Penn State men’s soccer will look for redemption against Michigan State and honor the late Mack Brady during this home memorial match.

The “Mack Brady Match” is held every year during the fall season to honor the late Mack Brady, who once dreamed of becoming a Penn State goalkeeper. Brady, who passed at just nine years old, is remembered during this game and the match is a special part of the season each year.

This will be head coach Dow’s first memorial match with Penn State, and something he is honored to be a part of.

“I got to know very quickly Brady’s father and the legacy that he wanted to leave here in the Penn State soccer program and remember his son who passed away tragically,” Dow said. “These are the things that make a program special, so I hope we can put together a performance that the family’s going to be proud of.”

Previous play

Penn State’s current record sits at 2-3 while winless in conference play after falling to the Huskies, and will have to fight to go up against Michigan State’s 5-1-1 record. They struggled going against the experience of the Washington team, and will likely face the same struggle against the Spartans.

“A lot of respect for our team to go out there with a fearless mentality, but it just wasn’t enough. Right now Washington is better than us,” said Dow.

Despite the loss, freshman goalkeeper Daniel Peluffo-Wiese will be a key player for Penn State, having made eight saves, a career high for him against Washington.

“We left him up to dry; it was a great performance,” Dow said. “Best performance of the year: his kicking game, his box management, just some worldly saves.”

Soaring scoring

The blue and white will rely on Wiese to protect their box, as well as its offense to put the pressure on the Spartans and go against their offensive line up.

“They can score too; I think they do it differently, a little bit more transition, a lot more crosses into the box. We feel like we have good strengths in those areas with the two Sheridan’s and Förster,” Dow said. “I think it’s making sure when our duals are out wide from the defensive standpoint, but we need to overload our build-up a little bit more.”

Penn State will have to look out for senior forward Andrew Darakijan, after he scored his first goals of the season and the only goals in their latest win against Northwestern. Darakijan will be a match for Penn State’s Amadou Kone as both are tough on offense.

The blue and white will potentially see a different formation lineup, adding another player to their backline, in order to have someone open for a free pass. Dow also believes the team's biggest opportunity will be in the counterattack.

“If we can be relentless in this first and second-ball winning and then thinking more forward, which is a big emphasis this week,” Dow said. “I think we can keep the ball out of their feet and more into ours, and in their half and not ours.”

Penn State will look to improve its record and prove it is a fighting contender in the Big Ten this season, despite its new-look team.

title: Preview | Penn State men’s soccer to host No. 24 Michigan State
author: Sara Castrovinci | The Daily Collegian
description:
After suffering a loss to No. 11 Washington on Friday in Seattle, Washington, in its first conference matchup, Penn State looks to flip the script heading into its Big Ten home opener.

The Nittany Lions host No. 24 Michigan State on Jeffrey Field at 7 p.m. on Friday.

The last time the two teams met on the pitch was Oct. 3 during the 2025 season when the blue and white defeated the Spartans 2-1 at the DeMartin Soccer Complex on Michigan State’s home turf. Penn State leads the all-time series at 18-17-3.

In games played at University Park, the Nittany Lions lead 12-7 and in East Lansing 10-7-3. While Penn State holds a historical advantage regardless of location, Friday’s matchup on the blue and white’s turf gives Penn State a real edge against the ranked Spartans.

What to watch for Michigan State

The Spartans look to stay in the hot seat coming off a 2-0 clean sheet against Northwestern on Tuesday.

Michigan State’s Miles Merritt, Brandon Munson and Peter Soudan came into the season named Big Ten Men’s Soccer Players to Watch. Point contribution-wise this season, all three players are sitting at six points via two goals and two assists.

Andrew Darakdjian made his way to the top of the stat sheet, notching nine points via four goals and one assist. Leo Conneh and Luke Spadafora sit just behind Darakdjian, both with seven points via two goals and three assists.

Michigan State proves to have multiple offensive outlets who can create goal-scoring opportunities, forming a tough lineup against the Nittany Lions’ defense.

On the Spartans’ defensive side, Jake Grekowicz has started and played in all seven matches, tallying 11 saves and a 0.611 save percentage.

Altogether, Michigan State is a powerful unit, earning their No. 24 ranking at 5-1-1 for the season and a perfect record within the conference.

What to watch for Penn State

Heading into Friday’s matchup sitting at 2-3-0 for the season, The Nittany Lions look to reverse the trend and improve to a winning standing.

Senior forward Amadou Kone sits at the top of the offensive score sheet, tallying seven points via three goals and one assist. Sophomore defender Joe Sheridan is next in line with three points via one goal and one assist, showcasing his ability to be impactful not just in the back line but in the final third as well.

The blue and white have other offensive options after Kone and Sheridan. Beckham Brown, Joe Buckley, Sheridan McNish and Luca Sowinski all marked two points, providing Penn State with depth in their attacking threats.

Daniel Peluffo-Wiese continues to be The Nittany Lions’ main choice in goal this season, playing and starting in all five matchups. Peluffo-Wiese sits with 14 saves and a 0.560 save percentage, struggling to prevent opponents from converting their scoring opportunities.

While the blue and white found several contributors offensively, the team is yet to find defensive momentum to keep opponents off the scoresheet. Ahead of Friday’s action, Penn State looks to break out of its defensive slump and move above .500 on the season.

title: Penn State women’s soccer travels to face Maryland led by former Nittany Lion forward Jolie Farmer
author: Sara Castrovinci | The Daily Collegian
description:
After defeating Minnesota 1-0 Sunday at Jeffrey Field in its second Big Ten matchup, Penn State looks to stay in the win column heading into its third conference game.

The Nittany Lions travel to face Maryland on Ludwig Field at 5 p.m. on Friday.

The last time the two teams met on the pitch was Sept. 11 during the 2025 season, when the then-No. 8 blue and white defeated the Terrapins 4-0 at Jeffrey Field in their Big Ten opener. Penn State takes its all-time series record to 18-4.

Maryland looks to overcome its historical struggles with the Nittany Lions heading into this week's matchup.

What to watch for Maryland

The Terrapins look to snap their losing streak this Friday after suffering back-to-back road losses to Washington, 2-0, and Oregon, 1-0. Maryland is sitting at 3-4-1 for the season but has found consistent struggles within the conference at 0-2.

Former Penn State forward Jolie Farmer has emerged as Maryland’s primary offensive threat. The redshirt sophomore has tallied the most points for the Terrapins this season, totaling nine, much higher than any of her teammates.

The Tampa native has accounted for four of the Terrapins’ seven goals and one of its two assists. Farmer’s familiarity with the Nittany Lions may provide Maryland with an added advantage in the upcoming matchup.

After Farmer, Payton Bernard, McKinley Heaven and Ella Petry are tied with one goal apiece. Heaven has recorded the most shots on the season at 18, potentially deeming her a second creator for offensive opportunity alongside Farmer.

On the defensive end, Meredith Fisher and Faith Luckey have been sharing time in front of the net with a total of 11 goals allowed in eight games and a team save percentage of .711.

The Terrapians will look to take advantage of its home-field success against Penn State where they are 3-1 on the season.

What to watch for Penn State

Penn State is coming into Friday hot off of their Minnesota win but has shown to struggle in its away games.

The Nittany Lions haven’t shown much offensive power since their matchups against Bucknell, 5-0, and Brown, 6-0, two impressive clean sheets. Aubrey Kulpa provided one of the blue and white’s biggest attacking threats in recent matchups, including Ohio State, where the junior forward applied consistent offensive pressure while trying to erase the Nittany Lions’ 1-0 deficit, but was unable to find the back of the net.

The Cromwell, Connecticut, native leads Penn State in points at nine via three goals and three assists. Nicole Crane and Paige Kalal have made their way up in the standings, with Crane sitting at three goals and one assist and Kalal at two goals and two assists.

Despite recent offensive struggles, the blue and white defense has continued to show strength throughout the season. Redshirt senior Kayleigh Herr, the cornerstone of the Nittany Lions’ lineup and defensive veteran, as well as redshirt sophomore Lily Burger, have maintained a formidable back line.

The blue and white will look to pair their strong defensive foundation with more offensive production this Friday against Maryland, building off their win over Minnesota.

title: No. 9 Penn State women’s volleyball to close nonconference slate against South Florida, No. 16 Tennessee
author: Elliott Inscho | The Daily Collegian
description:
Riding a four-match winning streak, No. 9 Penn State is set to finish its nonconference slate with a pair of home matchups against South Florida and Tennessee this weekend.

Led by a dynamic duo of Kennedy Martin and Whitney Lauenstein, who have averaged 3.52 and 3.25 kills per set, respectively, Katie Schumacher-Cawley's squad has dropped just a single set in the stretch of victories.

The weekend series against the Bulls and Lady Volunteers will be the final opportunities for the blue and white to tune up before Big Ten play begins with a trip to Michigan on Sept. 25.

Penn State last faced South Florida in last season’s NCAA First Round, when the Nittany Lions took down the Bulls in four sets. Martin led the way in that match with 22 kills and 3 aces, but the blue and white were swept in the next round to end their campaign.

So far this season, South Florida looks far different than last season’s playoff team. The Bulls are 1-7, with their lone victory coming in a sweep over Utah State on Aug. 30.

Outside of that win, they’ve only won four sets all season. South Florida has faced some tough competition, falling to No. 3 Kentucky, No. 4 Stanford and No. 11 TCU, but coach Jolene Shepardson’s group has also dropped matches to the likes of Eastern Kentucky, Marquette and Dayton.

First-year outside hitter Paula Tomasa leads the Bulls with 3.82 kills per set on the year, and the Bell Ville, Cordoba, Argentina, native earned American Conference Freshman of the Week honors after leading the conference with 46 kills on a .314 hitting percentage.

Despite the Bulls’ sub-par record, Schumacher-Cawley noted that she isn’t overlooking them in the playoff rematch.

“[The] expectations are to play well and to win on home court,” Schumacher-Cawley said on Tuesday. “They'll compete. They're a very good team. I expect it to be a great match, but I know we'll be prepared and use these next couple days to get ready for the weekend.”

Penn State is 4-0 all-time against South Florida. The fifth meeting’s first serve is set for Friday at 6 p.m.

A significantly tougher test is to come on Sunday. Tennessee sits at No. 16 in the latest AVCA poll, boasting a reciprocal record to the Bulls at 7-1.

The Lady Volunteers were untouchable to start the season, winning their first 15 sets to jump out to a 5-0 record. It wasn’t strictly against bottom-feeders, either, as Tennessee picked up a ranked sweep over No. 21 Indiana in the stretch.

A trip to the Steel City halted the unblemished run, as a sweep by No. 2 Pitt handed the Volunteers their first loss in Kissimmee, Florida.

Tennessee rebounded in a major way by sweeping Coastal Carolina and Queens. Aside from the loss to the Panthers, the Lady Volunteers have yet to drop another set all season. Before facing off with Penn State on Sunday, they’ll take on South Florida in a neutral-site game at Rec Hall.

Penn State’s block will have its hands full against Kennedi Rogers, as she’ll undoubtedly be the biggest weapon that they’ve had to handle all season. The 5-foot-10 outside hitter ranks No. 3 nationally with 4.89 kills per set, trailing only LSU’s Jurnee Robinson and Pitt’s Olivia Babcock.

Rogers’ squad boasts a powerful all-around attack that leads the country with 15.14 kills per set. They also rank seventh nationally with a .327 team hitting percentage.

Sunday’s match will feature a pre-match block party before first serve at 2 p.m. It’ll be match No. 11 in the all-time series between Penn State and Tennessee, with Penn State holding a 6-4 lead.

The Nittany Lions have won five of the last six matches between the squads, dating back to 1985.
