title: Big Ten roundup | Michigan, Rutgers draw chatter, 4 head coaches make Big Ten debut
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
College football is back.

The Big Ten was featured in 18 games in Week 1, ranging from Friday to Sunday with a wide variety of outcomes, including Michigan’s miraculous victory, a loss from Rutgers and more.

Here’s a look at the action taking place across the conference last week.

Michigan’s last-second victory

One of the biggest storylines across college football this week came from No. 16 Michigan’s last-second victory over Western Michigan.

After leading 7-6 at halftime, the Wolverines gave up a field goal early in the fourth quarter to give the Broncos a 9-7 edge with 10:45 to play. With 35 seconds on the clock, Western Michigan split the uprights with another field goal, leaving Michigan needing a touchdown to win.

Following the kickoff, sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood threw a pair of incompletions before a 28-yard pass had Michigan in field goal range. With nine seconds left, Underwood scrambled in the pocket and tossed up a last-second Hail Mary, which fell incomplete as the clock ran out.

Officials ultimately put one second back on the clock — as Western Michigan’s defender touched the ball after stepping out of bounds — prompting Underwood’s 47-yard touchdown pass for the win. Michigan fans then stormed the field after avoiding an upset.

Head coaching debuts

In addition to Matt Campbell’s Penn State debut victory over Marshall and Kyle Whittingham’s win for Michigan, two other head coaches led their teams for the first time this weekend.

Pat Fitzgerald took the field with Michigan State on Friday night to face Toledo. The first quarter was dominated by the Spartans with a 13-0 lead, including a rushing touchdown from UConn transfer Cam Edwards.

The Rockets came alive in the second quarter with a 60-yard passing touchdown from quarterback John Alan Richter, but were quickly stopped by another pair of field goals from the Spartans. Things got interesting to start the second half as Toledo scored a pair of touchdowns to take a one-point lead, but ultimately fell after the Spartans scored 11 points in the fourth quarter.

Across the country in California, former James Madison coach Bob Chesney made his debut with UCLA on Saturday night.

Through three quarters, the Bruins and California were neck and neck, with Nico Iamaleava struggling to find the end zone in the passing game. However, a pair of rushing touchdowns from Wayne Knight and a 53-yard rushing score from Anthony Woods in the fourth quarter sealed the deal, giving Chesney an opening 45-24 victory.

Rutgers’ upset loss

UMass was paid $1.5 million to face Rutgers in Week 1, according to Brett McMurphy of On3. Less than 20 minutes into the contest, the Minutemen were up 14-7 and never looked back, winning 37-21.

The Minutemen had 397 yards of offense, only 48 yards more than Rutgers. However, the Scarlet Knights gave up four turnovers, allowing UMass to control the scoreboard.

KJ Duff’s incredible performance was the only highlight for Rutgers, as its star wide receiver had 196 yards and three touchdowns.

Close nonconference victories

While many teams scheduled easier nonconference opponents, No. 2 Oregon and No. 17 Washington opened with two of the tougher games last week.

The Ducks hosted Boise State, a team that is two years removed from a College Football Playoff semifinal appearance against Penn State. Oregon barely held on to defeat the Broncos 34-27.

Despite the near loss, Heisman hopeful Dante Moore began his 2026 season with 378 passing yards and three touchdowns.

The Huskies, meanwhile, faced interstate rival Washington State, defeating the Cougars 24-10.

Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. led Washington’s offense to just 10 points through three quarters, but the defense held Washington State off the board for 50 minutes.

Five minutes into the fourth quarter, Caden Pinnick found the end zone for Washington State, making it a three-point game.

Eventually, the Huskies found some offense and pulled away, with Pinnich throwing his second interception to seal the game late in the fourth quarter. Washington has now won four of the last five Apple Cups.

title: Recruiting roundup | Penn State welcomed high number of recruits for Stripe Out crowd
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
In Matt Campbell’s first game at Penn State, he brought in a plethora of recruits, spanning from the 2027 to 2029 classes, as he and the staff continued preparing for the future of the program.

A number of current commits returned to Happy Valley, while others stepped into Beaver Stadium for the first time.

From highly touted recruits to top committed players, here’s a look at who showed up for Week 1 and what it could mean for their future recruitment.

Returning commits

Multiple players who’ve committed to Penn State attended the opening game of the season.

Cornerbacks Kei’Shjuan Telfair and Ka’ron Ceaser, safety Caleb Cooper and offensive lineman Ryan Robbins all were in town, all of which are currently members of the Nittany Lions’ 2027 class that currently ranks No. 24 in the country, according to 247Sports Composite.

Joining them from the 2028 class were quarterback James Armstrong and cornerback Deonte Flemings Jr., both in-state talents. Flemings is expected to take visits elsewhere this season, but remains strong in his commitment to the Nittany Lions.

While early in the cycle, the 2028 class is currently No. 3 in the country behind Alabama and Ohio State.

Pushing early in 2028

Penn State may add one or two more players in the 2027 class, but it’s clear that the staff has already started pushing for 2028 talent.

The 2028 class could be a big class for Penn State, which is already making moves for some of the top players in the country.

The top cornerback in the class, 5-star Nasir Richardson, made his way from Newark, New Jersey, to Penn State for Week 1. Richardson’s in a growing pipeline, with the Nittany Lions having more players from New Jersey committed than from Pennsylvania in the 2027 class.

Richardson ranks as the No. 11 player in the country and the top player in the state to begin his junior season of high school. Penn State got in early with an offer on Jan. 31, but the 6-foot cornerback holds offers from all the top teams in the country, with six Big Ten schools extending an offer in the first half of May.

Joining Richardson was 3-star wide receiver Ketih Nolen Jr. and 3-star defensive back Lawrence Diggs, both from the DMV area. The recruiting in the region took a massive hit following the loss of Ty Howle, who followed James Franklin to Virginia Tech.

3-star running back Juelz Chiron-Robinson made his way from the Philadelphia area for the game after getting offered by Penn State on June 20. The Downingtown East product is planning to return to Happy Valley for the White Out game against USC on Oct. 10 and could be an early target at running back in the 2028 class.

The 2029 class featured two headlining names in attendance for the 45-0 victory over Marshall. 247Sports 4-star edge rusher DJ Dockery visited from Washington D.C., an area Penn State has familiarity with, as former offensive tackle Olu Fashanu and current freshman running back Jeremy Washington are alumni of the Gonzaga College High School in the nation’s capital.

Additionally, linebacker Bam Pelzer was in attendance. The high school sophomore stands at 6-feet-1, 210 pounds with likely time to grow more, but he already holds a college body type at the linebacker position. Pelzer has offers from many of the major programs including Oregon, Texas A&M and Notre Dame.

Flip candidate

Penn State could add to its 2027 class in the near future, with a potential flip from someone committed to an ACC program.

3-star defensive lineman McCoy Richardson visited over the weekend and received an offer on Sunday. The No. 7 player in Massachusetts received a crystal ball to flip from Wake Forest to Penn State from 247Sports national recruiting analyst Brian Dohn following the visit.

Richardson fits the new mold for the defensive line, standing 6-foot-3.5, 300 pounds, joining the bigger interior defensive linemen on the current roster and the two commits in the 2027 class. He fits the size that defensive line coach Ikaika Malloe has looked for.

The Massachusetts native would be the third interior defensive linemen in the class and the 23rd player in the overall class if he flips to the Nittany Lions before Early National Signing Day in the beginning of December.

Whether you’re looking for a space to discuss the newest episodes of your favorite anime, play in a recreational sports league or try out a new hobby, the Involvement Fair is the best way to kick off a new school year.

Everyone knows how it feels when your situationship from last semester passes you in the HUB during the first week of classes and pretends not to know you, right?

Take those pent-up feelings and unleash them at the State Theatre this Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. with a showing of the timeless classic “Pride and Prejudice.” The 2005 adaptation has everything needed in a historical romance — beautiful people, enemies to lovers and passionate confessions.

Another event that was postponed due to rain, State College’s annual block party, Lion Bash, is now taking place from 5 to 8 p.m. on South Allen Street. The event has a wide variety of vendors ranging from DJs to food trucks to music and dancing.

With activities suitable for all ages, Lion Bash is the perfect spot to dive into the State College community and discover what makes Happy Valley special.

Need to dance out the beginning of the school year jitters? Ella Langley’s “The Dandelion Tour” is making a stop in the Valley to perform her hit songs “Choosin’ Texas,” “Be Her” and “You Look Like You Love Me.”

Happy Valley Latin Festival

The sixth annual Happy Valley Latin Festival is returning to State College this Saturday at the MLK Jr. Plaza from 11 a.m to 6 p.m.

Enjoy artisanal products from Latinx community members, live music, salsa, tango and more. This community led event is a great opportunity to meet new people and enrich yourself in the different cultures that make up the Happy Valley.

title: Off the Record | That’s just how guys are
author: Miss Behave I The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor’s Note: Off the record is a weekly column written by a fourth-year Collegian staffer writing under an alias. It aims to promote a space for honest conversations about love, sex and relationships. Those interested in sharing their experiences or submitting a topic are invited to do so through this anonymous form.

“That’s just the way college guys are.”

I’ve heard this sentiment several times, and I can’t help but notice a glaring flaw in it. If college guys don’t want to commit, only want girls for their bodies and never see them for more than sex, then why are so many Penn State women constantly getting into relationships? It’s not “just the way guys are.” Clearly, the “problem” is us single ladies. Right?

There are some women in college who seem to find relationships left and right. Others say no to sex and aren’t given the time of day. It’s disheartening to be wanted only for your body when your heart is so full of love.

Why do we continuously make excuses for guys? We’ve all heard, “If he’s mean to you, it’s just because he likes you,” or, “Boys will be boys.” These phrases have been ingrained into women’s minds since childhood, and perpetuate harmful messages to young women and men.

I’m sick of it. And that’s OK. We don’t need to justify our feelings with poor excuses for men. In fact, we can just feel all the emotions we please.

I don’t have an answer for why some girls face the feelings of only being seen and wanted for sex while other girls attract relationships full of depth and reciprocal love. (Not to say any of this is easy for them, by the way).

Is it the circles we hang out in? What we do for fun? Who we’re attracted to? Or is it simply just how our stories were written?

Of course, we can love our friends who have been lucky in love, but they don’t necessarily understand the feeling of actively trying to cultivate a healthy relationship, only for the other person to just want sex.

They don’t necessarily understand the feeling of becoming a shell of yourself, separating your sexual life from your mind to feel wanted in the only way you’ve ever been.

This feeling is extremely isolating, but you’re not alone. It’s expected for a man to not want commitment. After all, it’s “just how college guys are.” The ironic thing is, when a woman wants sex without commitment, she’s considered a whore.

Sometimes, you might just think, “What’s wrong with me? Why am I good enough for sex but nothing more?” Society has deemed a whore to be a woman — I think we all know that. After all, when we’re referring to a man, we say man-whore instead.

Women aren’t supposed to want sex. We’re supposed to want the flowers. But why can’t we want both? A woman who wants sex is a whore, a slut, she gives off “a vibe.” She has no self-respect or dignity. A man who wants sex? Well, that’s “just how guys are.”

Women are expected to want relationships, and men are expected to want sex. As a woman, I wonder: when a girl won’t sleep with a guy, do his friends tell him, “that’s just how college girls are?” I’m going to say the answer is no.

Rules don’t exist when it comes to hooking up. If you want a relationship, it doesn’t mean you have to wait to have sex. If you want to wait, you should. There are more pressing issues than how a woman decides to live in her body.

Even so, the guilt that can arise from participating in hook-up culture as a girl wanting a relationship can be painful. I’ve seen the quote “I’ve given my body more times than I’ve been given flowers” across social media platforms. Watching guys walk downtown with bouquets on Valentine’s Day after searching Trader Joe’s for the perfect selection of roses, the feeling isn’t necessarily jealousy.

Women don’t always want this so-called reassurance. They don’t necessarily want to hear “love comes from within yourself.” They don’t want to hear that their time will come. I won’t tell you any of these things — they’re cliché and lack substance.

I think the most important thing for women who feel they are only seen for sex to understand is: you’re so worthy of love, there’s nothing wrong with you and you’re not alone.

I also want to say that you can do whatever the hell you want; it’s your body, your life. I’ll be here cheering you on the whole time.

Yours truly,

Miss Behave

MORE OFF THE RECORD

title: Brooklyn Bodega Deli and Grill | Bringing New York to State College
author: Talia Rittenhouse | The Daily Collegian
description:
Brooklyn Bodega Deli and Grill recently opened up on 340 E. College Ave.

Here, the bread and bagels come straight from New York, bringing authentic, delicious meals to State College. As a girl whose parents are from the New York area, I just knew this restaurant would hit home.

Not only are there sandwiches and bagels, but you can also buy pancakes, French toast, omelets and platters for breakfast, and salads, fries and burgers for lunch or dinner.

Let me tell you, this is not a place you want to miss out on — Brooklyn Bodega has just become one of my go-to spots.

Chopped Cheese

Wow — this may be better than any other burger.

If you love the gooey cheese on a cheeseburger, just imagine you have that in every bite. With the hamburger meat chopped up — hence the name, “Chopped Cheese,” you truly get that cheesy goodness in each bite you take.

You also have lettuce, tomato and onion in every bite. With the cheese, you don’t even need a condiment to dip the burger into, although it never hurts to add more flavor.

There was a perfect amount of seasoning in this dish, and the lettuce was kept fresh and not soggy, like some fast food chain burgers you might have had in the past. So without a doubt, this could be one of the best burgers I’ve had — you’re truly missing out if you don’t grab this for your next meal.

Chicken Parm Sandwich

Another one you cannot pass up.

The classic Italian dish, chicken parmesan, turns into a sub, hoagie, sandwich — whatever your family taught you to call it.

You always need a good roll for this kind of meal. It’s chewy and flavorful and holds together all of the ingredients without losing its structure.

In each bite, you get layers of breaded chicken and delicious marinara sauce. The kind of sauce you would get at a nice Italian restaurant, but here it is, at our new bodega in State College.

And again, this sandwich has melted cheese all within, adding extra flavor in each bite, pulling all of the ingredients together from everyone’s favorite dish.

Bacon Cheese Fries

Truly, how could you ever go wrong with these three key ingredients — cheese, bacon, fries, what’s not to like?

The fries themselves have a great seasoning and crunch to them, so if cheese fries are not your style, you can still get them on the side of any other order.

If I had to change one thing about this, and I mean had to, it would be cutting the bacon up into smaller pieces so you could have more across the plate of fries, but still, this side is close to perfect.

Imagine getting bacon cheese fries after a long day of college football tailgating or as a late-night snack — now that’s ideal.

Bagel

After talking with the workers in the store, I learned that their bagels come straight from New York, so if you're from New York or New Jersey, you may get a taste of home at the Brooklyn Bodega.

The bagel was on the sweeter side and had an amazing chew to it, a factor that is a must-have in a bagel.

However, I did miss the crunch factor from the outside, but this could be fixed with a double toasting.

The bagel was not my favorite I’ve ever had, but I would definitely be open to trying it again, especially as a bacon, egg and cheese.

Waffle Egg and Cheese

At Brooklyn Bodega, you can get an egg and cheese on many different things — on a bagel, pancake, french toast or a waffle.

Seeing these unique options, I had to give this one a try since it was different from anything I’ve heard of.

After having a few bites, I realized I may not be a fan of mixing sweet and savory foods with one another, but that doesn't mean it wouldn’t be someone else’s favorite.

You get the savory from the egg and melted cheese and then a taste of sweetness from the waffle holding it all together.

If you’re more adventurous than me with trying foods like this, you should venture into one of these breakfast options.

title: Penn State women's volleyball moves up to No. 12 in AVCA rankings
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:

title: Penn State men’s hockey's new-look numbers for 2026-27
author: Maggie Hardy | The Daily Collegian
description:
College hockey returns in just over a month, with a new class gearing up to make their Hockey Valley debuts.

New names on the roster also mean new-look numbers scrawled across the classic blue and white sweaters for the 2026-27 season.

Here’s a look at the jersey numbers the newest Nittany Lions will be wearing ahead of their first appearances at Pegula Ice Arena.

History makers

Before last year, the highest number a Nittany Lion had worn was No. 35.

In a historic 2025-26 season, Penn State seemed to do away with its shortened number system, allowing this summer’s No. 1 overall NHL draft pick, Gavin McKenna, to wear No. 72, and standout sophomore forward JJ Wiebusch to claim No. 86, to name a few.

After last season’s changes opened the door, four new blue and white skaters will be the first in program history to wear their chosen numbers this year.

A big addition to Penn State’s forward core was Maine transfer forward and 2024 fifth-round NHL draft pick Justin Poirier, who will be the first to wear No. 89 for the Nittany Lions.

Forward Andrew Kuzma will make his return to Hockey Valley this season, this time suiting up with No. 91. After the discovery of an undetected medical condition forced Kuzma to redshirt his freshman season back in 2024, he spent last season in the OHL before recently returning to Penn State’s roster.

Finally, freshmen Shea Busch, a Florida Panthers 2025 fourth-rounder, and Justin Larose, a forward out of the QMJHL, will don No. 74 and No. 96, respectively.

Out with the old, in with the new

Three newcomers have elected to step into the shoes of the recent graduates, claiming numbers previously worn by 2025-26 Nittany Lions.

Former Penn State defender Carter Schade’s No. 2 will be passed down to fellow blueliner and Vermont transfer Caeden Herrington. Herrington was another big get for the blue and white out of the transfer portal this offseason, taken in the fourth round of the 2025 NHL draft by the Los Angeles Kings.

Freshman Crew Petty is keeping No. 35 within the goaltender family, taking over former Nittany Lion standout goaltender Kevin Reidler’s number after he signed an entry-level contract with the Ottawa Senators.

To round out the trio, former Miami (OH) defenseman Charlie Michaud claimed former forward Alex Servagno’s No. 8.

Bringing back the past

The remaining five skaters are bringing back numbers that have been out of rotation for the past few seasons.

One of Penn State’s most exciting new recruits is reigning OHL goaltender of the year Ryder Fetterolf, who will be wearing No. 1 for the blue and white for the first time in over a decade, since it was worn by fellow goaltender PJ Musico during the 2014-15 season.

Tampa Bay Lightning draftee Marco Mignosa is bringing back No. 26, last worn by Penn State forward Ashton Calder during the 2022-23 season.

Defenseman Ethan Weber, No. 6, forward Kaden Pitre, No. 17, and forward Kale Dach, No. 22, all selected numbers last worn by blue and white alumni during the 2024-25 season to finish off the list.

title: No. 12 Penn State women’s volleyball earns sweep over DePaul, closing out Midwest road trip
author: Myles Hannak | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State concluded its time in the spotlight at Wrigley Field, ‘woo wap da bam’ and got back in the win column in Chi-Town.

The Nittany Lions visited a packed McGrath-Phillips Arena on DePaul’s campus and ultimately earned a gritty sweep to improve to 4-1 on the season.

Blue and white coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley sent out a first unit of Alexis Stucky, Ryla Jones, Kennedy Martin, Gabrielle Nichols, Haley Burgdorf, Whitney Lauenstein and Ava Falduto, who slid into the starting group for the first time this season.

That group couldn’t prevent an early DePaul onslaught, as an opening ace to start the match’s scoring signaled what would be to come. The Demons cruised to a 6-1 lead, forcing a Penn State timeout, and doubled up the score toward the midpoint of the set.

Nittany Lions’ star right-side hitter Martin started slow, logging her first kill to cut the deficit to 13-7, as the blue and white attempted a clawback catalyzed by her offense. The senior logged two more kills and assisted another as Penn State drew within four of the Demons, as freshman Finley Krystkowiak joined in with her own pair of kills.

Despite it looking like a long shot to win the set, Penn State eventually cruised back to do so with a score of 25-23 via strong play at the net from the defense led by Jones’ four total blocks. Martin and Lauenstein led the offensive charge with five kills each after the first set, as Krystkowiak added three kills and a pair of block assists.

Finishing the set on six straight points didn’t lead to any gassing out from the Nittany Lions as they started the second set with a trio of points, highlighted by a Stucky ace. Just as the lead led to a doubling up of the score before things tied, that exact same fate occurred as the Nittany Lions' lead quickly dwindled to a 13-13 deadlock.

Into the second set, coach Schumacher-Cawley extended her lineup, as she used Lexi Gin, Jocelyn Nathan and Krystkowiak with much more frequency. Despite the change in personnel on the floor, the offense still flowed through Martin via her kills, as DePaul outmatched the Nittany Lions in serving. The Demons logged four aces when Jones logged Penn State’s second, which tied things at 19 as the set remained back and forth.

The Nittany Lions got into a set point situation after a block, but surrendered a kill to cease the advantage before a pair of blocks from each side knotted things at 25. Penn State earned a point on a DePaul attack error before Stucky and Jones combined for the set-sealing block to go up 2-0 in the match.

Martin logged four kills over the set, while Lauenstein and Burgdorf both had three. The Demons were neck and neck in most statistical categories and remained a real pain in the side of the blue and white, yet the timely attacking efficiency and defensive prowess at the net allowed Penn State to sit comfortably entering the third set.

The Nittany Lions fell behind early in their attempt at a sweep, yet a trio of kills from Burgdorf brought the deficit within one before Lauenstein recorded three consecutive kills to seize an 8-7 lead and force a DePaul timeout. Coach Schumacher-Cawley sent out freshman Kendall Northern to start the set, who rotated in as a substitute throughout its duration.

That break didn’t do much to aid the suffering for the Demons, as Penn State navigated to a five-point lead to force another DePaul stoppage for a regrouping. This time it helped DePaul’s chances, as blocks and misplayed attacks from the Nittany Lions allowed things to once again reach a tied score.

Penn State appeared to take the deadlock as motivation, logging five straight points to claim match point. Among the scoring barrage, Stucky logged a pair of aces to bring her total to three on the day, and Lauenstein had a pair of kills. DePaul logged a kill to end the scoring streak before Lauenstein elevated with a kill to finalize things, yet a challenge from the Demons showed the ball was untouched, overturning the score.

The time the refs spent at the video board only extended things, as Jones floated a ball over the net for the decisive kill as soon as play resumed.

In the win, Martin posted 15 kills on a .333 hitting percentage, joined by Lauenstein with 17 kills on the same hitting percentage. Freshman outside hitter Burgdorf also finished with a career-high eight kills, hitting for a .545 percentage.

Up Next

The blue and white stay on the road, then return to the Commonwealth with a neutral-site contest against Stanford on Friday. Start time is slated for 6 p.m.

title: Former Penn State fullback, Super Bowl champion Matt Suhey dies at 68
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Longtime NFL veteran, Super Bowl champion and former Nittany Lion Matt Suhey died on Saturday.

Suhey died in his sleep Saturday night at 68-years-old, according to the Chicago Tribune.

The former Penn Stater was selected by the Chicago Bears in the second round of the 1980 NFL Draft. He appeared in 148 games for the Bears, playing a big role in the team's 1985 Super Bowl title.

Suhey scored the team's first touchdown in the championship against the New England Patriots. During his 10-year career, he rushed for 2,946 yards and recorded 20 rushing touchdowns.

With the Nittany Lions, Suhey recorded 2,818 yards on the ground and 26 rushing touchdowns from 1976 to 1980.

title: Penn State women's volleyball to finish Chicago swing against DePaul
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
After Penn State’s main event at Wrigley Field last night, the encore performance comes at 4 p.m. against DePaul. The Nittany Lions face the Blue Demons less than 24 hours after a draining 3-1 loss to SEC favorite Kentucky.

Senior Kennedy Martin led the charge offensively against the Wildcats with 16 kills, but 27 attack errors sank the Nittany Lions.

So far this season, graduate student Whitney Lauenstein and the inevitable Martin have been an impressive offensive duo with over 40 kills each.

Florida transfer Alexis Stucky is the team’s far and away leader in assists and racked up 27 assists, six blocks and nine digs in her Rec Hall debut against UConn. Her connection with Lauenstein and Martin will be key as the blue and white readies itself for a much different environment than it saw last night.

It’ll be a sellout crowd inside DePaul’s 3,000-seat McGrath-Phillips Arena when the No. 13 Nittany Lions come to town. This will be DePaul’s second-straight matchup against a top-15 Big Ten opponent.

The Blue Demons were 4-0 before they ran into No. 1 Nebraska’s buzzsaw on Friday. Before the resounding sweep, DePaul ran through Milwaukee, Drake and South Dakota in the Drake Invitational, then followed its undefeated opening weekend with a win over Portland State.

In the match against Nebraska, the scarlet and blue kept the first set close, working to a 13-13 tie. However, the Cornhuskers closed the set on a 12-6 run and blitzed the rest of the match. Sophomore Kenall Timme led DePaul in kills the same way she has all season.

Timme, the 2025 Big East Co-Freshman of the Year, led the Blue Demons in kills last season as well and now additionally leads her squad in service aces with nine.

DePaul brought in five new players to complement its 13 returners for 2026. That group is headlined by All-CAA honoree Leonor Polezzi.

Polezzi, a Cortona, Italy, native, spent two seasons at North Carolina A&T, where she led the 2025 Colonial Athletic Association in assists per set with 10.26 as well as service aces. The setter is now tied with Timme as DePaul’s service aces leader.

Timme, Polezzi and the rest of the Blue Demons are not Kentucky, but they will serve as a challenge for the Nittany Lions as they look to leave the Windy City with a victory.

title: No. 13 Penn State women's volleyball falls to No. 3 Kentucky in Wrigley Field
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
No. 13 Penn State traveled to Wrigley Field in Chicago to take on No. 3 Kentucky on Sunday night.

The Nittany Lions couldn’t pull off the upset, falling to the Wildcats in four sets for their first loss of the young season.

The beginning of the match didn’t seem to show the 10 rank gap between the two squads, as they were neck in neck the entire first set.

The first set was a game of kills. Penn State’s Kennedy Martin totaled six kills, specializing in finding holes in the Wildcats front line blockers. While Martin appeared to dominate, Kentucky’s own Morgan Gaerte responded efficiently.

Gaerte constantly gave the Wildcats their best point of attack, while totaling three kills in the first set. Senior outside hitter Brooklyn DeLeye contributed four kills of her own. While DeLeye started off slow, picking up two errors, she helped in closing out the set, contributing three of the final four points in the 25-23 set win.

Throughout set two, Kentucky junior Kennedy Washington put up a stubbornly physical front to challenge Penn State’s front outside hitters. Washington also did her part of the offense, putting up two kills.

DeLeye’s momentum from the final four points of set one traveled over to her second set, as she put up eight kills.

For the blue and white, Martin continued with the hard hits, while also finding space in the middle of the Wildcat defense for soft placements in the center of the floor. The 6-foot-6 right-side hitter used her shifty style to make it hard for Kentucky to predict where she would place the ball.

Nittany Lions redshirt senior Alexis Stucky also stepped up to lead hand in hand with junior Ryla Jones. The duo completed paired blocks to shut down offensive runs for the Wildcats. Jones’ discipline and ability to read the opposition let her efficiently clog the holes where Kentucky had previously been capitalizing.

While this slowed Kentucky down early, Gaerte’s kills helped the Wildcats persevere through the pressure, ultimately closing out the second set with a 25-21 win.

Martin’s kill game remained consistent in the third set, making it difficult for Kentucky to escape with an easy sweep. While Gaerte’s swings proved to pose a steady challenge for the Nittany Lions, as she used her power for cross-court attacks, Jones and Stucky put up a competitive front.

These big swings made it difficult for Penn State to catch up, and it began relying on a more defensive game play for a majority of the match. This was until graduate student Whitney Launstein began to fuel the fight following a blue and white timeout in the middle of the third set.

Launstein responded with cross-court swings and two kills, resulting in a seemingly 180-degree switch in Penn State’s energy, all to get within one point.

Launstein continued Penn State’s rally to take the lead as she contributed a total of two blocks, three digs and twelve kills by the end of the third set. This show-out performance allowed the blue and white to take the lead and forced Kentucky to call a time-out in an attempt to halt the Nittany Lions’ contagious energy.

While Kentucky slowly crept back after this run, Penn State finished the set off with a 25-23 victory thanks to a Jones kill, ultimately keeping the Nittany Lions alive for a fourth set.

Martin’s performance remained consistent in the fourth set, achieving a 15 kill sum by the second Penn State point.

The DeLeye-Gaerte duo remained dangerous, Gaerte focusing on blocks, while DeLeye continued to put up dangerous counterattacks.

Penn State challenged Kentucky’s block on Martin’s hit. After review, it was confirmed that DeLeye touched the ball on Martin’s hit, giving Penn State its ninth point of the set. Regardless of the challenge, the Nittany Lions’ momentum was low, and their play needed to be cleaned up in order to close the point gap.

From here on out, it was all Wildcats.

Kentucky was able to gain a 10-point lead toward the end of the match. Launstein attempted to give the Nittany Lions life, but nothing could slow down the Wildcats’ dominant fourth set. Sophomore Georgia Watson’s kill gave Kentucky their 25th point, to take both the 10-point set win and the match as a whole.

Up Next

Penn State will remain in Chicago to play DePaul at McGrath-Phillips Arena at 4 pm, Monday.

title: Stock up, stock down | Penn State WR Koby Howard shines, top running backs slip in Week 1
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State’s season opener against Marshall on Saturday is in the books, as the Nittany Lions cruised to a comfortable 45-0 victory over the Thundering Herd.

The first win under Matt Campbell was a dominant one, but although there were a host of positives, there are some areas of concern to think about for the future.

Here’s who’s making an early impact and who’s not living up to expectations.

Stock up: Koby Howard

With all of the talk in the offseason surrounding Taylor Mouser’s tight end room, the Thundering Herd put a lot of emphasis into stopping that unit. However, all that did was open up space for the wide receivers to shine.

Koby Howard was the star of the show. He accumulated 161 receiving yards and a touchdown on six catches as the first Nittany Lion to surpass the 150-yard mark since Parker Washington in 2022. It wasn’t all through the air, as Howard had 76 yards after catch.

“Going out there, being able to actually do it in the game, and not just in practice,” Howard said postgame. “A lot of people probably think of just doing it in practice, but being able to showcase it in the game really meant a lot to me.”

James Franklin’s staff would speak on Howard’s capabilities last season, but never truly gave him a chance to shine until Terry Smith took over as interim head coach. Howard had seven catches in nine games for 133 yards.

It was clear Howard was going to get a bigger role under Campbell very early on this offseason, and he capped off the break by being named as one of Mouser’s MVP’s of fall camp. He showed why he earned that title on Saturday.

Stock down: Running backs

While the passing game succeeded, the running game faltered, primarily because the Thundering Herd loaded the box, doing everything in their power to stop the running backs.

It resulted in a very underwhelming day for the room’s debut. Carson Hansen and James Peoples were both scoreless while the starters were on the field, averaging 4.4 and 3.9 yards per carry, respectively. The team totaled 163 rushing yards on the afternoon.

There were moments where Peoples’ shiftyness potentially got the better of him, as he slipped a couple of times, causing Rocco Becht to look for a wide receiver instead. Such a moment led to Howard’s first touchdown, which was originally a play designed to hit Peoples on the flat.

Quinton Martin Jr. and Cam Wallace produced more on the scoreboard in the second half, each getting into the end zone, and the two Penn State returnees showcased a more consistent flow.

But the room overall still didn’t offer the explosive rushing offense that many have come to expect out of Penn State.

Stock up: Caleb Bacon

Caleb Bacon was a starting linebacker at Iowa State before following Campbell to Happy Valley. At the beginning of fall camp, however, Bacon made the switch to the defensive end, and there was uncertainty in the air of how he’d perform in that debut showing.

It’s safe to say that he outperformed expectations. Although he didn’t start, Bacon was the top edge rusher with six tackles, three tackles for loss and a sack.

“If you go back to Bacon’s last two years, there was a lot of multiplicity in what he did there,” Campbell said. “The reality is this guy has earned the right to become a great player, and he was a great player in the past. Sometimes he doesn't get the recognition like everybody else.”

Bacon was everywhere on the field, and there were as many as four defensive ends on the field at the same time, giving him the opportunity to attack from different angles.

It made for strong blitz packages that didn’t give quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson or Marshall’s offensive backfield enough time and space to make plays.

Stock down: Zion Tracy

Zion Tracy was one of Campbell’s most hyped up players this offseason. Campbell even said that Tracy has been “one of the best football players I’ve coached” this spring.

For a player with so much talent on the football field, it took the stadium by surprise when Josiah Zayas, a true freshman, was announced as a starting cornerback instead of Tracy.

Tracy did have a splint on his left hand, which could’ve factored into the decision to leave him out of the starting lineup, but he played great football regardless of his health status. The senior led cornerbacks with five tackles.

However, Zayas had a solid outing as the starter, making two tackles, two tackles for loss and a quarterback hurry. If Zayas continues to establish himself as a top cornerback on the team, Tracy’s role as a bonafide defensive superstar could see limitations.

Stock up: Young defenders, turnovers

Campbell also worked a lot of his depth pieces into the game in the second half, and many of those younger players made a quick impact on the stat sheet.

Both of Marshall’s turnovers were to true freshmen, with Bryson Williams snagging the first interception of the season on backup quarterback Zion Turner’s first throw and defensive end Jackson Ford recovering a fumble late in the fourth quarter.

“Ford has done a really good job through spring ball and then in the season, you're gonna have to fight to get yourself into a position at the defensive end,” Campbell said on Aug 20. “I think Jackson can help us in some other ways too.”

title: Penalty corners take center stage as Penn State field hockey beats Delaware for 3rd straight win
author: Owen Lomotan I The Daily Collegian
description:
Following their 2-0 home win over Villanova on Friday, Penn State field hockey aimed to make it three straight victories against the Delaware Blue Hens on Sunday.

The Nittany Lions did just that with a 2-1 victory; however, the win was defined by more than the final score. Penalty corners became the biggest factor in the game's flow, giving Penn State repeated opportunities to generate offense while also forcing its defense to withstand the Blue Hen attack.

Penn State was awarded three penalty corners in the first quarter, with two taken by junior forward Ella Gaitan and another by sophomore defensive back Lilly Holmes. None found the back of the net, but the early opportunities established a pattern that continued throughout the afternoon.

With 13 minutes left in the second quarter, Gaitan finally converted one of those opportunities, giving Penn State a 1-0 lead. The Nittany Lions earned two more penalty corners before halftime, taken by Gaitan and sophomore forward Joji Purdy.

Gaitan's goal remained the only score before halftime, but Penn State's ability to create chances from penalty corners helped keep pressure on Delaware. The Nittany Lions also limited the Blue Hens to just two penalty corners in the opening half.

Delaware came out of halftime with a response. Junior goalkeeper Aby Deverka blocked a shot just 45 seconds into the third quarter, but the Blue Hens eventually found the tying goal through fifth-year midfielder Alexa Michielsen with just under 14 minutes remaining.

For Deverka, the key was remaining composed after giving up the goal.

“Just knowing that my teammates expect something of me and I expect something of myself,” Deverka said. “Just staying grounded with that, staying composed. When I had that one goal against, I was immediately okay, next one, so what can I do to help us with this game.”

Penn State's penalty-corner opportunities continued to provide an answer. After another chance by Holmes came up empty, Gaitan found the net again with 12:14 remaining in the third quarter, giving the Nittany Lions a 2-1 lead.

The goal proved to be the difference.

Delaware continued to challenge Penn State defensively and earned several penalty corners of its own, but Deverka and the Nittany Lion defense repeatedly prevented those opportunities from becoming goals.

Within the last 10 minutes of regulation, both teams were awarded two penalty corners. On the defensive end, Deverka and sophomore defensive back Cooper Cutchins came up with crucial blocks inside the circle. On the offensive end, Gaitan and Purdy were unable to convert their opportunities, leaving Penn State with its one-goal advantage.

“We knew that Delaware was just a very competitive program, it’s a new team this year. We didn’t know a lot going into them,”Deverka said. “We saw that they beat No.18 Monmouth, and we’re like okay, we need to put respect on their name. Just going into this, we had our gameplan and we just stuck to it.”

Coach Hannah Prince emphasized the importance of players like Deverka making those late-game plays.

“[Deverka] got recognition after our last game for our hard hat hero award just for being really solid with her intensity, with her presence, stepping up in clutch moments so can’t say enough good things,” Prince said. “[Deverka] works her butt off, she demands from her teammates, she’s just one of those kids that isn’t afraid to say the hard things that is hard to hear but is inevitably going to help us.”

The win gives Penn State three straight victories and provides another example of how the Nittany Lions can use penalty corners to create opportunities while relying on their defense to protect narrow leads.

Penn State will now welcome No. 2 Princeton to Happy Valley at noon on Sept. 13.

“I think for the first couple days, we’re gonna focus really on us,” Prince said. “Having a full week before our next game allows us the opportunity to really go back to the drawing board of what we need to do first and then the adjustments we need to see in our own play regardless of our opponent.”

For the Nittany Lions, the focus heading into the week will remain on improving the details of their game while maintaining the identity that has helped them win three straight.

“There’s the X’s and Os, and there’s the fitness component and the penalty corner component of the game, but to us, being true to our values, staying humble, being a blue-collar team,” Prince said. “This year, we’re an underdog; we’re not ranked, but we have the ability to compete with any team in the country.”

Up Next

The Nittany Lions return to action at home next Sunday with Youth Day & Alumni Day, as they host Princeton. Start time is slated for noon.

title: Week 1 report card | Penn State’s offense produces success, defense generates shutout against Marshall
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State’s season opened on Saturday with a shutout victory over Marshall, starting Matt Campbell’s tenure off on the right foot.

Between a dominant performance from wide receivers to Rocco Becht’s debut in Beaver Stadium, the Nittany Lions had a strong showing across the board.

Here’s how I’d grade the different aspects of Penn State’s game in Week 1.

Overall grade: A-

Coaching staff: A

Campbell’s Penn State debut couldn’t have gone much better. He became the first Penn State coach with a shutout in their first game since 1915 and made a pair of fourth down conversion calls that proved fruitful.

The coordinators and assistant coaches also made the most of their available players with several depth players unavailable. They were able to play a bunch of different guys, giving them meaningful reps.

Offense: B+

Against a Sun Belt conference opponent, the Nittany Lions succeeded with the passing game alone. However, the run game was a major issue that was never able to develop.

Quarterbacks: A-

If this rating was on Becht alone, it would be an “A.” His Penn State debut produced 271 passing yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers.

In relief, Alex Manske was solid with a 75% completion percentage. Connor Barry, meanwhile, had two of his three plays go backwards.

Passing game: A

The lack of contributions from the tight ends, as Benjamin Brahmer and Andrew Rappleyea recorded just one catch each, might’ve decreased this grade any other week, but the absolute dominant performance from the wide receivers helped keep the “A” rating.

Koby Howard’s performance was lights out, tallying 161 yards and a touchdown. Combined with touchdowns from Brett Eskildsen and Zay Robinson, the Nittany Lions’ passing game flourished.

Rushing game: C+

The rushing game was arguably the worst aspect of Saturday’s performance for the Nittany Lions. The two leading running backs, Carson Hansen and James Peoples, didn’t find the end zone, while Quinton Martin Jr. and Cam Wallace did score as Penn State ran the clock out.

The Nittany Lions averaged 3.6 yards per carry on the ground.

Offensive line: A-

Becht had all the time in the world on numerous drives, including Howard’s first collegiate touchdown, and allowed just one sack all game.

Defense: A

Penn State’s defense kept Marshall off the board for 60 minutes, which was a testament to D’Anton Lynn’s playcalling.

The other reason for celebration was the lack of big plays from the Thundering Herd. Their biggest rush was for 10 yards, while their longest reception went for 14 yards.

Pass rush: B

Caleb Bacon’s switch from linebacker to defensive end seemed to pay off, finishing the day with a sack and a team-high three tackles for loss. However, the rest of the defensive line didn’t contribute much, as Penn State tallied just two sacks on the day.

Defensive backfield: A-

Through two drives, Penn State’s defense allowed just 14 yards, with six coming through the air. Zion Tracy and Josiah Zayas made several big plays on defense.

The Nittany Lions allowed just 103 passing yards on the day and tallied an interception late in the game off backup Zion Turner.

Linebackers: A-

After tearing his ACL last season, Rojas returned to Beaver Stadium as one of the best defenders of the day. With seven tackles, two tackles for loss and a sack, he was a primary key to the shutout.

Kooper Ebel — who was wearing the green dot — started off with several flashes and finished the day with three tackles and half a tackle for loss. Meanwhile, Cam Smith and Cael Brezina finished with four and five tackles, respectively.

Special teams: A

The only area Penn State’s special teams would be docked is Nathan Tiyce’s one touchback. However, the group had many good moments against Marshall, including 6-for-6 extra points and a 38-yard field goal from Ryan Barker, a downed punt at the 1-yard line and Robinson averaging 13.7 yards off his three punt returns.

title: ‘No surprise to us’ | Penn State DE Caleb Bacon makes name for himself at new position
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Defensive end Caleb Bacon joined Matt Campbell at Iowa State in 2021 as a walk-on before becoming a player who started every game with the Cyclones in 2025.

On Saturday, Bacon made a name for himself in his first game at Penn State and debuted as a defensive end, finishing second on the team with six tackles in the Nittany Lions’ win against Marshall.

“That might have been a little bit of a surprise to some fans,” linebacker Kooper Ebel said postgame. “Just seeing a new face out there, but man, that's no surprise to us. He's been doing that for a long time, and we're super happy.”

Bacon joined Penn State as a linebacker and worked at that spot through the spring and summer before testing out the waters as a defensive end to start fall camp. The move caught Bacon “off guard a little bit,” but his ability to “buy in” and trust the coaching staff has already paid dividends.

“The coaches I'm surrounded with, d-line coaches, really all of them have really bought into trying to make me a better player, and I really appreciate them for doing that,” Bacon said.

The quick adjustment came as no surprise to Campbell, who recognized Bacon’s work ethic following a season-ending injury in 2024. Bacon’s resilience to come back from that showed Campbell the type of player Bacon is and can become.

It came to fruition in Bacon’s first snaps as a defensive lineman, where in back-to-back plays he tackled Marshall quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson behind the line of scrimmage.

“I think you guys got a chance to just see a little bit of just how special a player this guy is. He's tough. He's worked for everything he's got,” Campbell said.

Bacon had some experience playing up on the line of scrimmage at Iowa State, but that was in special schemes where he was moved to the edge. Now in D’Anton Lynn’s scheme, it’s the opposite, where he’s up on the line every play and will occasionally drop back into coverage.

The adjustment is something new to Bacon, but a change that he’s adapted to well. Ultimately, the play calling from Lynn “put us in great positions” for success against Marshall, leading to three tackles for loss for Bacon.

Bacon attributed his big game to his positional group. The change to defensive line came just over a month ago, and he’s already making a difference on the field, proving to be another chess piece for Lynn’s sometimes chaotic scheme.

“The d-lineman just took me in, been able to watch film with the guys in there, coaches, players, all of them, just learn what it takes to be a really good defensive lineman,” Bacon said.

title: Penn State cross country opens season sweeping Dolan Duals
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
While Penn State lost several of its top runners from last season due to graduation, it still performed at the top of its game in 2026.

The Nittany Lions opened the season against Lock Haven at the Dolan Duals on Friday, winning the men’s race 15-48 and the women’s race 15-50.

Here’s a look at how the blue and white took home the opening meet of the 2026 season.

Men’s 5,000m

Sophomore Isaac Opperman led the way for the men’s team after being one of the only true freshmen to compete last season. Against Lock Haven, he earned his first career victory, running 15:27.3.

Fellow sophomore Adam Kingston, who also saw action last year, finished a little over a second behind with a time of 15:28.7.

Brian DiCola was the first upperclassman to finish for either team, crossing the finish line in 15:33.8 for third place.

Freshman Thomas Rae finished fourth overall and was one of four freshmen to race for Penn State. He crossed the finish line in 15:34.3.

Woodland Hills, California, native Dorian Bening finished fifth for the Nittany Lions in a photo finish against Rae. He was another one of Penn State’s freshmen, finishing in 15:34.6.

Lock Haven junior Jakob Rager was the first athlete crossing the finish line for the Bald Eagles, finishing in sixth place. Less than half a second behind him was the third of the freshmen, Colin O’Donnell, who ran 15:35.2 for seventh place.

The Nittany Lions earned 15 of the top 18 spots in the race, including freshmen Justin Landis in 16th place.

Women’s 5,000m

Following a rising junior campaign, Claire Zubey earned her first cross country victory, running 17:29. She was followed by freshman Vivian Kipruto, who was five seconds behind in 17:34.

Sophomore Caroline Tribett competed in her first non-redshirted race on Friday, finishing third in 17:36.

A sizable gap followed Tribett, led by graduate Runner Katie Dallas. She continued Penn State’s sweep with a fourth-place finish, running 17:47.

The freshmen success continued as Gwynedd Valley, Pennsylvania, native Reese Miller finished less than a second behind in 17:50.

After an ankle injury limited her production during the second-half of the spring, graduate student Charlotte Costich finished sixth overall with a time of 17:57.

UNC Charlotte transfer Ella White rounded off the top-seven for the Nittany Lions as she crossed the finish line in 18:03 for her blue and white debut.

Anna Bondy was the last of the freshmen to race for Penn State, running 18:21 for 10th place.

The women’s squad took the first 12 places, with Lock Haven’s first runner coming in at 13th place.

Up next

The Nittany Lions will compete at the Harry Groves Spiked Shoe Invitational at Penn State, starting at 10 a.m. on Sept. 11.

title: ‘The sky’s the limit’ | Penn State WR Koby Howard’s breakout performance comes after offseason of hard work
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Koby Howard’s first catch of the 2026 season was a 42-yard touchdown reception. The sophomore found a wide-open gap in Marshall’s coverage and caught Rocco Becht’s pass at the 25-yard line before turning on the jets to outrun a pair of trailing defenders.

Howard had handed Penn State its first touchdown in the Matt Campbell era.

Those 42 yards were a fraction of his impact on the field. By the time he was taken off the field in the third quarter, he’d racked up 161 yards on six receptions, making him far and away the Nittany Lions’ top receiver to open the season.

“Going out there, being able to actually do it in the game, and not just in practice,” Howard said after the game. “A lot of people probably think of just doing it in practice, but being able to showcase it in the game really meant a lot to me.”

Arguably Howard’s defining play of the game was his last. Backup quarterback Alex Manske had recently checked in, and he let loose a lofting, 25-yard pass to Howard, who was under heavy pressure.

Howard jumped high in the air with his arms reaching over the defender’s head, snagging the ball and tumbling to the grass just inside the 15-yard line.

The Stripe Out crowd exploded in a chorus of cheers for a catch that set up Penn State’s fifth touchdown of the afternoon.

“I was like, ‘holy cow, no one's guarding him,’” Manske said. “I was trying to get a snap off. There ended up being a guy that ran out at the last second. I really didn't see him. When I put it in the air, I had a pretty good idea that Koby was going to come down with it. That was a crazy play, and that's the stuff Koby does.”

What made Howard truly effective was his ability to gain additional yardage after the reception. Of those 161 total receiving yards, 76 of them were earned after the catch by making swift cuts and burning the secondary with his speed.

Howard said this trait was “harped on a lot” at training camp by coach Kashif Moore.

For Howard’s teammates and coaches, the wide receiver’s performance was a result of the commitment and effort he displayed throughout the entire offseason.

Wide receiver Brett Eskildsen said that Howard’s breakout on Saturday was “only a matter of time.” Eskildsen put in a lot of effort getting to know Howard, and the pair trained with each other out in California and Florida.

“I've seen him work from the day I got here, and just being able to build that relationship together, I knew it was coming,” Eskildsen said after the game. “Whether it was today, next week, whenever it was coming, it was coming. It's unbelievable to see, it's well deserved and it didn't surprise any of us.”

Despite being promoted as one of the top receiving prospects last season, Howard barely saw the field under James Franklin but appeared in nine total games with 133 total receiving yards.

Howard surpassed that number in one game.

In an effort to take a step forward this year, Howard arrived at the training facility at 5:15 a.m. throughout the offseason to catch passes from the JUGS machine. Campbell has taken notice of that work ethic, and knew his opportunity would come soon enough.

However, Campbell also said that it’s important for Howard to remember that games like this one won’t happen every time. He noted that his ability to stay in the present will be huge for his development going forward.

“The sky’s the limit for Koby Howard,” Campbell said. “I’m really proud of him because it’s a great reward. Koby’s a guy that’s worked hard behind the scenes to take advantage of those moments. He’s got a chance to have a really special year for us.”

title: ‘That had nothing to do with me’ | Matt Campbell celebrates 1st Penn State victory crediting players, staff
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
As the team drove up Porter Road to Beaver Stadium, Matt Campbell wasn't the first person off the bus to greet the fans. He wasn't even the first coach off the bus.

Campbell’s Penn State debut featured the same humility he’s portrayed since he arrived in December. From the arrival off the bus to his postgame press conference, he continued to show that this isn’t about himself as a coach, but about the team and players he leads.

“You look up and you see those teams on our press box and some of the great coaches and players that played here, you’re just grateful to have the opportunity to lead a football team and continue to try to represent our fan base and the past of this program the right way,” Campbell said.

Campbell kept the focus off himself throughout his postgame press conference and on the field. He deferred a question asked about his personal emotions in Game 1 to talk about the assistant coaches and the team, and he de facto sprinted off the field so he could greet every player walking into the locker room.

His focus on the players was seen on the videoboard pregame as well. Campbell opted not to be announced alongside his starting lineup, saying with a laugh postgame “Yeah, I’m good on that. The scoreboard’s for the players.”

For some players, Campbell is the reason they’re at Penn State in the first place. Specifically, Alex Manske, who had his first action since open heart surgery, said that Campbell is why he transferred from Iowa State to the Nittany Lions.

“It means everything to me,” Manske said. “Following (Campbell) here, that was the goal the whole time because I knew what he could install in his program with the resources here.”

While playcalling was reserved for Taylor Mouser and D’Anton Lynn, Campbell’s focus was keeping the pace of the game and playing situational football.

Specifically, Campbell was tested with fourth downs today. He took a chance on a pair of fourth down conversions, electing to keep his offense on the field.

While the Nittany Lions converted both opportunities — resulting in touchdowns on both drives — Campbell took a risk on both chances.

“I’ll be honest with you, I didn’t know if that was a great call or not,” Campbell said with a laugh.

As Campbell walked away from Week 1 with a victory, marking the first Penn State coach with a shutout in their debut since 1915, he emphasized the importance of the families surrounding the program and pushed the credit away from himself.

“There’s a lot of young families that picked up and moved across the country because of their belief in what we were doing together,” Campbell said. “That had nothing to do with me. That was a we thing… (They’ve) really held a great standard in our program.”

title: ‘It felt great to be out there’ | Rocco Becht has efficient showing in Penn State debut
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Rocco Becht said Tuesday that “he might have a couple butterflies walking down the tunnel” prior to his first start in a Penn State uniform.

But Becht said postgame his stomach wasn’t fluttering as he expected. Instead, he was calm, and that coupled with his experience allowed him to have an efficient performance, going 13-for-18 with 271 yards and four touchdowns before being taken out in the third quarter in his Nittany Lions debut.

“I felt good. I honestly felt like I was gonna have a little more butterflies, and I was talking to some guys,” Becht said postgame. “It's probably because I'm a fifth-year dude, and so I'm a little older, so it felt normal to me. But it felt great to be out there.”

What Becht hadn’t experienced yet was a home entrance in Beaver Stadium, with his first coming in a Stripe Out environment with 108,489 fans behind him to begin the game.

“It was crazy to see everybody out there, the stripe fest that the fans were doing, and so to see the energy and feel the just environment and all was totally unique for me and different. So I was just excited to be a part of it,” Becht said.

Although the opening drive didn’t result in a touchdown, Becht showed his poise the next possession and got to experience his first Beaver Stadium crowd pop with a 42-yard throw to Koby Howard for his first touchdown pass at Penn State.

“Our running back fell getting out, which was probably where the ball was going to go,” Becht said. “ I had to move on. The o-line did a great job protecting me, and nobody was coming through. So we were able to do a kind of like an in-the-pocket scramble drill, and Koby did a good job of finding green grass.”

Becht’s first touchdown pass sparked the offensive momentum, leading to a dominant first half and proving there wasn’t any rust or kinks to be worked out despite the newness of the team.

The chemistry shown in the four-touchdown performance from the Nittany Lions’ quarterback was “a tribute to all the work and all the time he put into his craft” during the offseason, as wide receiver Brett Eskildsen put it.

Becht dished the ball to six different targets, finding both his wide receivers and tight ends during the game as the Nittany Lions raided Marshall through the air.

“I think for Rocco to be able to handle that and distribute the ball, sometimes being a great quarterback is like being a great point guard, right?” Campbell said. “You got to be a great distributor of where the ball needs to go, and I thought he was outstanding today.”

Becht’s final touchdown pass of the day came on Penn State’s first drive of the second half with a bullet to his former Iowa State teammate Zay Robinson capping off his first showing in Beaver Stadium.

The touchdown pass in the third quarter gave Penn State a 31-0 lead, and allowed Becht to fully take in his first experience with a full crowd at Beaver Stadium, allowing his backup Alex Manske to get some playing time.

“I think when I got pulled in the third quarter when my day was over, I think just taking it all in at that moment, knowing that I played my first game at Beaver Stadium,” Becht said. “The way that we did it, we did it at a smooth rate, a clean rate, no turnovers… I think everything just coming together as one, us going out there playing as one team was great.”

title: 3 takeaways from Penn State's shutout win over Marshall
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State began the Matt Campbell era in front of a Stripe Out crowd against Marshall Saturday.

The Nittany Lions gave the Happy Valley faithful plenty to cheer for as Penn State routed the Thundering Herd, 45-0, behind an emerging pass rusher and a huge game from Koby Howard.

Here’s three takeaways from Penn State’s opening game win.

Caleb Bacon's move to DE paid off

Caleb Bacon initially made the switch to edge rusher to begin fall camp as Campbell felt the team would be “missing the boat not to start him off in fall camp on the edge.”

Bacon’s move to defensive end became official on Aug. 30, and Saturday showed why he made the change.

The redshirt senior was the beneficiary of multiple unique schemes, featuring additional edge rushers throughout the defensive line. Bacon’s power, mixed with speed from the edge, proved to be a difference maker on multiple drives in the first half.

Bacon totaled six tackles, three tackles for loss and a sack, moving around the defense line in the opening half.

Penn State proved it could get to the quarterback, sacking Marshall quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson twice, while also stopping any running opportunities for the dual-threat quarterback. With Bacon’s performance, the pass rush adds even more depth and could be a big part to the Nittany Lions’ defensive production.

Wide receiver outburst

Campbell said at local media day that Penn State would likely be in 12 or 13 personnel on most occasions on offense. However, in the team’s first game, it was the wide receivers who created separation and connected with Rocco Becht.

The receivers were Becht’s go-to targets despite the hype surrounding the tight ends during the offseason. Howard, Brett Eskildsen and Chase Sowell all made key catches and big plays to get Penn State out to a big lead in the first quarter.

It was Howard, however, who emerged as Becht’s top target in the first half.

Howard’s first reception of the season went for a 42-yard touchdown after Becht found him wide open in the middle of the field. Howard totaled 81 yards in the first quarter and 123 in the first half.

The sophomore proved he can do it all with another catch in the middle of the field before making people miss. He capped off his game with a catch over top of a defender, ending with 161 yards, more than he had in all of 2025.

Eskildsen and Zay Robinson also got in on the receiving parade, both catching touchdown passes from Becht.

The tight ends totaled just two catches, in comparison to 14 from the wide receivers, before Campbell deployed the backups in a blowout. Benjamin Brahmer did get on the board with a touchdown, though.

Running backs struggle

The biggest position group to be affected by the outburst from the receivers was the running backs, and when they got their chance to move the ball, they didn’t produce.

Carson Hansen and James Peoples were the two backs to get action in the first half, but neither was consistent.

The duo combined for 18 rushes and 73 yards, totaling just over four yards per carry. On one drive, Peoples was given three straight carries and couldn’t get the first down, gaining nine yards.

It wasn’t until Quinton Martin Jr. came into the game in the second half that Penn State showed signs of consistently running the ball well. Martin and Cam Wallace each ran in a 6-yard rushing touchdown, but none of the running backs could put together consistency.

While the running game’s struggles didn’t make a difference in the final score, if it continues this way, it could come back to hurt the Nittany Lions later in the season.

title: Penn State names captains for Week 1 against Marshall
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State's captains have been named for Week 1.

Offensive lineman Anthony Donkoh, quarterback Rocco Becht, linebacker Kooper Ebel and long snapper Blaise Sokach-Minnick were announced to be the captains for the season-opener against Marshall.

Becht and Ebel have prior experience as captains on a game-by-game basis at Iowa State, while Donkoh and Sokach-Minnick are debuting their "C."

Last year, Penn State's captains were named for the full season. However, Matt Campbell brought his game-by-game policy to Happy Valley.

"That might be a thing where we put finality to that probably, maybe even a little bit later in the season," Campbell said Wednesday. "It's a unique time in this team, and I think there's a lot of guys that certainly you know maybe deserve the right to be that, especially when you saw the vote from our football team. So I think we'll just kind of navigate that probably one game at a time as we get into it."

The Nittany Lions will face Marshall on Saturday at Beaver Stadium at 3:30 p.m.
